title: Size-Independent Robustness in Multipartite Bell Self-Testing
abstract: Practical robust self-testing of multipartite entanglement has so far been restricted to small-scale systems due to error bounds that degrade severely with system size. In this work, we establish multipartite self-testing with robustness independent of the size of the quantum network. We derive a fully analytic, device-independent self-testing bound for $n$-qubit Greenberger-Horne-Zeilinger (GHZ) states. The bound scales linearly with the observed violation error and lies universally within a constant factor of two from a theoretical upper bound. Furthermore, the operator-inequality framework reduces the verification of the conjectured optimal bound to a highly efficient numerical check, which we perform up to $n=100$. Consequently, GHZ entanglement can be certified under a fixed noise level in arbitrarily large systems, enabling scalable device-independent verification.

title: Pretrained, Curriculum-Tuned, and Ensembled: A Tracer-Aware Interactive Segmentation Pipeline for AutoPET V
abstract: Interactive lesion segmentation in whole-body PET/CT requires a model to provide a strong initial prediction while also responding efficiently to sparse corrective scribbles during inference. This setting is particularly challenging because tracer distributions, physiological uptake patterns, lesion appearance, and acquisition characteristics differ substantially between FDG and PSMA studies. We present TRIAGE, Tracer-aware Refinement via Interactive Anatomy-Guided sEgmentation. The core backbone is a 3D STU-Net initialized through masked autoencoding pre-training with an asynchronous masking strategy, aiming to learn transferable anatomical and cross-modal representations before task-specific fine-tuning. In parallel, we train an auxiliary organ segmentation model whose predictions provide explicit anatomical context and help distinguish physiological uptake from malignant lesions. A dedicated tracer classifier first routes each study to an FDG- or PSMA-specific branch. Within each branch, a first-stage segmentation model consumes CT, PET, and organ context to generate an initial lesion mask. The initial prediction is then combined with cumulative foreground/background scribbles and refined by a second interactive segmentation network. The FDG and PSMA branches share the same overall processing pipeline but are trained independently to account for tracer-specific appearance and error modes. We additionally employ curriculum-style training and model ensembling to improve robustness across interaction steps and heterogeneous cohorts. Experiments are conducted using the official AutoPET V data and ten-fold split; quantitative results, ablations, and final test-set performance are left as placeholders to be completed after the challenge evaluation. Code: https://github.com/Liiiii2101/AUTOPET2026-MEDAI.

title: Doc-REFRAG: Rethinking Multimodal Document Retrieval-Augmented Generation
abstract: Real-world knowledge resides in multimodal documents, necessitating retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) for accurate question answering. However, existing multimodal RAG models are primarily designed for single-image or closed-document settings and exhibit limited accuracy in realistic multi-image scenarios. Moreover, processing numerous retrieved images incurs substantial computational overhead from irrelevant visual tokens. To address these challenges, we introduce DocLongRAG, a large-scale dataset of 343K question--answer pairs, each associated with an average of 37.4 retrieved images to reflect authentic RAG workflows. Building on this dataset, we propose Doc-REFRAG, a question-guided framework that compresses visual tokens into coarse chunks and selectively expands question-relevant ones via a lightweight RL-based selector. Experiments on six benchmarks show that Doc-REFRAG outperforms eleven strong baselines, achieving state-of-the-art accuracy with significantly lower inference latency. Our resources are available at https://github.com/Collab-Gen/Doc-REFRAG.

title: Sublinear Space Graph Algorithms in the Continual Release Model
abstract: The graph continual release model of differential privacy seeks to produce differentially private solutions to graph problems under a stream of edge updates where new private solutions are released after each update. Previously known edge differentially private algorithms for most graph problems including densest subgraph and matchings in the continual release setting only output real-valued estimates (not vertex subset solutions) and do not use sublinear space. In this paper, we leverage sparsification to address the above shortcomings for edge-insertion streams. Our edge differentially private algorithms use sublinear space with respect to the number of edges in the graph. In addition, for the densest subgraph problem, we output edge differentially private vertex subset solutions; no previous graph algorithms in the continual release model output such subsets. We make novel use of sparsification techniques from the non-private streaming and static graph algorithms literature to achieve new results in the sublinear space continual release setting. This includes algorithms for densest subgraph, maximum matching, and the first continual release k-core decomposition algorithm. To complement our insertion-only algorithms, we conclude with polynomial additive error lower bounds for edge-privacy in the fully dynamic setting, where only logarithmic lower bounds were previously known.

title: Comparative Performance Analysis of SVM, LSTM, and IndoBERT for Sentiment Analysis of User Reviews
abstract: The Maganghub Kemnaker National Internship Program, launched on October 1, 2025, attracted significant public attention while also generating both criticism and praise on the social media platform X. This study compares the performance of three classification algorithms—Support Vector Machine (SVM), Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), and IndoBERT—for sentiment analysis of public opinions regarding the program. The dataset consists of 6,825 Indonesian-language tweets collected between October and December 2025 after duplicate removal. The data were preprocessed and labeled as positive, neutral, or negative using two approaches: automated labeling with a Hugging Face model and manual annotation. Each algorithm was evaluated under five hyperparameter tuning scenarios using an 80:20 train–test split and assessed with accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score. The results show that IndoBERT achieved the highest performance, with an accuracy of 85.27% using the Hugging Face–labeled dataset, outperforming SVM (79.05%) and LSTM (78.68%). IndoBERT's superior performance is attributed to its Transformer-based architecture and multi-head self-attention mechanism, which effectively capture bidirectional contextual information, including sarcastic expressions commonly found in social media posts. The findings were further implemented in a web-based dashboard to support interactive public opinion monitoring for policymakers.

title: A Combination of Forward Chaining and Certainty Factor Methods in a Child Mental Health Expert System with Accuracy Comparison Using the Strengths and Difficulties Questionnaire
abstract: The increasing complexity of child mental health issues requires accurate detection and intelligent decision-support systems for early identification and intervention. This study analyses emotional and behavioural difficulties among 500 children aged 11–17 years using the Strengths and Difficulties Questionnaire (SDQ) dataset and develops an expert system integrating Forward Chaining and Certainty Factor methods. Results indicate that most respondents had relatively low difficulty levels across SDQ dimensions, although substantial proportions showed high Emotional Symptoms and Conduct Problems scores, suggesting potential psychological concerns. The proposed expert system achieved 90% accuracy, demonstrating good performance in distinguishing Normal and Abnormal categories, although classification of the Borderline category remained challenging. Higher scores in Emotional Symptoms, Conduct Problems, Hyperactivity, and Peer Problems, alongside lower Prosocial Behaviour scores, were associated with greater likelihood of Borderline or Abnormal classification. These findings demonstrate that integrating Forward Chaining and Certainty Factor can effectively support early screening and decision-making in child mental health assessment.

title: Role of Artificial Intelligence in Financial Fraud Investigations: A Critical Review.
abstract: Abstract: AI significantly influences the financial fraud investigations across different parts of the workflow related to detection, automation, transactions prioritization, anomalous discovery, and fraud investigation explanations. This approach has documented highest performance metrics across empirical studies, to support detecting fraud in a set number of parameters. Random assessment gave up to 96% Accuracy (with a 98.9% Area under the curve); fuzzy logistic regression provides an AUC up to >0.99, with up to 0.90+ Sensitivity and Specificity on credit-card. Fraud investigation explanation AI ensemble “FraudX AI” provides 95% Recall and a 97% AUCPRC” (Afriyie et al., 2023; Baisholan et al., 2025; Charizanos et al., 2024). Machine learning cut unexpected losses by 15% compared with static heuristics. Meanwhile economic optimization showed a further reduction in expected losses and produced false positive rate of 0.4 percent (Vanini et al., 2023) which shows, that machine intelligence actually carries some operational weight once it predicts results in a financial decision. Although some performance measures that are heterogeneous among studies such as - a variety of approaches does not include specificity (often called precision), sensitivity (sometimes referred to as recall, or true positive rate), expected lost value added (often denoted by false positive burden, that for financial decision tasks refers to economic value) is frequently missed from reporting. None of the surveyed machine learning applications has achieved reasonable industrial applicability from their authors own perspective, except that there are few surveyed approaches which for an assessment of scalability and reliability are reported with reasonable degree of success in an industrial environment. (Ryman-Tubb et al., 2018). Explainability appears to be the furthest behind in Anti money laundering (AML) applications with 51% of machine learning models under review being categorized noninterpretable and no documented application of explainable AI reported at the time of writing in AML literature (Kute et al. 2021). On the whole AI best functions as a support in an investigation, not a tool that replaces auditor, compliance officer or investigation. Its effectiveness is related to managing class imbalance, dealing with dynamic fraud profiles, using privacy-preserving methods for data sharing, accurate labelling and obtaining evidence that can be understood by humans and is verifiable institution-to-institution, jurisdiction-to-jurisdiction.

title: 基于自适应的神经元网络的强化学习算法
abstract: This paper presents a novel reinforcement learning (RL) algorithm based on adaptive neuron networks, designed to automate the learning and parameter adjustment of neural network structures. The core innovation lies in a dynamic parameter adjustment mechanism driven by environment feedback, coupled with an adaptive learning process that optimizes the network's topology. The algorithm aims to improve the efficiency of reinforcement learning by reducing the reliance on manual tuning and promoting more robust and adaptable neural network configurations. We analyze the algorithm's performance across diverse tasks and demonstrate its effectiveness in achieving significant improvements in training speed and generalization ability compared to traditional RL methods.

title: Adaptive Compression Techniques for Streaming Data
abstract: This paper addresses the limitations of traditional compression algorithms when applied to streaming data, which inherently exhibits dynamic and variable statistical properties. The core idea presented is a novel adaptive compression technique that leverages machine learning to dynamically adjust its compression parameters in real-time. The algorithm learns from the incoming data stream, identifying and adapting to shifts in statistical distributions. This approach aims to achieve significantly better compression ratios compared to static compression methods, particularly in scenarios with non-stationary data. The paper details the architecture of the adaptive compression system, the machine learning model used for parameter optimization, and a theoretical analysis of its performance. The key contribution lies in the real-time adaptability, enabling the system to maintain optimal compression efficiency even as the data stream evolves. The proposed system is expected to improve data transmission efficiency and reduce storage requirements for streaming applications.

title: Adaptive Threshold-Based Deep Learning Model Optimization
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to optimizing deep learning models by employing an adaptive threshold mechanism within the loss function. Traditional deep learning models often rely on fixed thresholds, which can hinder the model's ability to effectively converge and generalize. The proposed method dynamically adjusts the threshold based on the progression of the training process, aiming to improve both the model's generalization capability and training efficiency. This adaptive thresholding strategy addresses the limitations of static thresholds, providing a more nuanced and responsive optimization process. The core claim of this work is centered on designing this self-adjusting threshold mechanism, while the core mechanism involves dynamically modifying the loss function's threshold during training to enhance model generalization and training speed. This research offers a potential improvement in deep learning model training, particularly in scenarios where the underlying data distribution changes or where a more sophisticated optimization strategy is required.

title: Self-Supervised Learning for Discovering Graph Embeddings
abstract: Graph neural networks (GNNs) have achieved significant success in various graph-related tasks, including node classification, link prediction, and graph classification. However, a critical limitation of many GNN approaches is their dependence on large amounts of labeled data for training. Obtaining such labeled data can be costly, time-consuming, and often impractical, particularly for large and complex graphs. This paper proposes a novel approach to learning graph embeddings using self-supervised learning (SSL). We hypothesize that intrinsic relationships within a graph structure can be leveraged to learn informative embeddings without relying on explicit labels. Our method utilizes self-supervised tasks designed to exploit the graph's connectivity and structure. Specifically, we explore techniques like contrastive learning and masked node prediction to learn embeddings that capture the underlying graph topology. We demonstrate that our self-supervised approach can learn effective graph embeddings, achieving comparable or superior performance compared to traditional supervised methods when labeled data is scarce. The key contributions of this work are the application of SSL to graph embedding learning and the design of novel self-supervised tasks tailored for graph data.

title: Quantum Topology and Machine Learning: A Hybrid Learning Algorithm
abstract: Quantum topology, a theoretical framework describing the properties of space and its connection to quantum mechanics, has emerged as a promising area of research with potential applications in various fields, including quantum computing and machine learning. This paper explores the integration of quantum topology with machine learning, specifically focusing on the design of a novel self-adaptive learning algorithm leveraging the unique characteristics of quantum computation. The core idea is to utilize the inherent adaptability of quantum systems to optimize the learning process, thereby enhancing model performance and efficiency. The presented approach aims to address limitations of traditional machine learning algorithms by incorporating quantum computational principles. This research investigates the potential benefits of such a hybrid approach, presenting a framework for leveraging quantum topology to accelerate and refine machine learning models.

title: Title: Non-Local Quantum State Synchronization via Wave Function Mirroring
abstract: Quantum information processing demands robust synchronization across distributed quantum systems. Current approaches often struggle with maintaining coherence over significant distances, limiting the scalability of quantum computations. This paper introduces a novel protocol, Wave Function Mirroring, designed to address this challenge by utilizing wave function mirroring to synchronize quantum states across multiple locations. The algorithm meticulously mirrors the evolution of quantum states, mitigating decoherence effects and facilitating distributed quantum computations with enhanced coherence. We present a rigorous mathematical framework and detailed implementation demonstrating the protocol's effectiveness in achieving synchronized states.

title: QUED V2 — Vom unproduktiven KI-Fehler zur viable Alternative
abstract: Abstract QUED V2 formalisiert die Mechanik, durch die KI Fehler von unproduktiven Abweichungen zu strukturierten, kognitiv verwertbaren Alternativen werden. Der Artikel zeigt, dass die Produktivität eines Fehlers durch zwei Faktoren bestimmt wird: die Komplexität des semantischen Raums und die Fidelity des kognitiven Transfers. Hohe Komplexität kombiniert mit hoher Fidelity erzeugt Fehler, die keine Fehlleistungen darstellen, sondern viable alternative Interpretationen. Durch wiederholte, ausgerichtete Divergenz stabilisiert QUED Bedeutungsräume, minimiert Drift, erhöht Auditierbarkeit und macht Sicherheit emergent. QUED V2 bildet damit die mechanische Grundlage für die in QUED V3 dargestellte angewandte kognitive Architektur.

title: Title: Geometric Modeling of Cognitive Processes
abstract: This paper explores the potential of utilizing geometric modeling to represent and analyze cognitive processes. The fundamental premise is that cognitive states, traditionally understood through complex neural networks, can be elegantly captured through geometric abstractions. We propose a framework wherein cognitive states are visualized as geometric objects – points, lines, surfaces, and more complex shapes – enabling deeper insights into brain function through visualization and analysis. This approach moves beyond traditional symbolic representations, offering a potentially more intuitive and readily interpretable model. We aim to demonstrate the utility of this framework for exploring and understanding various cognitive phenomena. The core mechanism involves translating abstract cognitive states into geometric forms, facilitating the identification of patterns and relationships that might be obscured by more complex neural network representations.

title: Dynamic Quantum Error Correction Code Optimization
abstract: This paper presents a novel algorithm for optimizing quantum error correction (QEC) codes, termed Dynamic QEC Code Optimization (DQCO). The core claim is to dynamically adjust both the encoding and decoding parameters of QEC codes to enhance their error correction performance. The proposed mechanism involves real-time adaptation of the encoding rate and decoding strategy based on the observed communication environment and noise levels. This approach strengthens the adaptive capacity of QEC codes, allowing them to better meet the demands of complex communication scenarios. The algorithm employs a feedback loop, continuously monitoring the channel characteristics and adjusting the QEC parameters accordingly. Mathematical formulations are presented to describe the optimization process, including the channel capacity estimation, the rate distortion function analysis, and the adaptive adjustment of the coding and decoding parameters. The results demonstrate a significant improvement in error correction performance compared to static QEC schemes.

title: Quantum-Inspired Simulated Annealing for Global Optimization
abstract: Simulated annealing (SA) is a widely used metaheuristic algorithm for global optimization, particularly effective in tackling complex, high-dimensional search spaces. However, SA's performance is often hampered by its susceptibility to getting trapped within local minima, significantly restricting its ability to discover the true global optimum. This paper proposes a novel quantum-inspired modification of the standard SA algorithm, termed Quantum-Inspired Simulated Annealing (QISA). QISA incorporates principles from quantum mechanics, specifically quantum tunneling and superposition, to augment SA's exploration capabilities. The core innovation lies in dynamically adjusting the temperature schedule based on probabilistic quantum effects, enabling the algorithm to more effectively navigate the solution landscape and escape local minima. The proposed approach is evaluated theoretically and through a detailed mathematical analysis, demonstrating its potential to significantly improve the convergence rate and solution quality for various global optimization problems. The algorithm's core mechanism relies on transitioning between states with a probability dictated by a quantum-inspired acceptance criterion, rather than solely relying on a fixed temperature schedule. This introduces an element of stochasticity and allows for more directed exploration of the search space. The evaluation results showcase a notable improvement over traditional SA in several benchmark problems.

title: Causal Graph Learning with Reinforcement Learning
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to causal graph learning leveraging the strengths of reinforcement learning (RL). Traditional methods for discovering causal relationships often falter when confronted with high-dimensional datasets and intricate feedback loops, frequently relying on assumptions that may not hold true in real-world scenarios. Our framework addresses these limitations by training an RL agent to iteratively construct a causal graph. The agent's actions involve modifying the graph – adding or removing edges – based on observed system behavior. The reward signal is determined by the accuracy of predictions made using the current graph representation. This integration of causal inference with RL enables the network to adapt and learn causal relationships within complex, dynamic environments, offering a potentially more robust and scalable solution compared to conventional techniques. We outline the core principles, the proposed agent architecture, and the reward function design.

title: Biafran Palm Squirrel: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Foraging Behavior of *Paraxanthoryctes krauzanni*
abstract: This paper presents a new metaheuristic algorithm, Biafran Palm Squirrel (BPS), inspired by the foraging behavior of *Paraxanthoryctes krauzanni*, a squirrel species endemic to the Biafra region. The algorithm mimics the squirrel's efficient search strategy for food resources, incorporating elements of exploration and exploitation. BPS utilizes a novel adaptive population management scheme, a modified Lévy flight mechanism, and a dynamic weight adjustment strategy based on the relative fitness of individuals. The algorithm's performance is evaluated on a range of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its competitive capabilities compared to established metaheuristic methods like Genetic Algorithm (GA) and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO). The results indicate that BPS is robust and adaptable, offering a promising alternative for tackling complex optimization challenges. The core of the algorithm revolves around maintaining a diverse population while strategically directing search efforts towards promising regions of the search space. We demonstrate its effectiveness through numerical simulations and analysis, highlighting its potential advantages in various applications.

title: 混沌域的自建领域优化算法
abstract: This paper presents a novel self-built optimization algorithm based on the concept of a chaotic domain. The algorithm leverages the dynamic nature of chaotic domains to rapidly adapt to varying system parameters, offering a potentially transformative approach to optimizing complex systems. The core mechanism centers around constructing a chaotic domain representation of the system's objective function, allowing for efficient parameter adjustment through iterative refinement. We explore the potential of this approach in the context of machine learning, demonstrating its effectiveness through simulations and preliminary experimental results. The paper concludes with a discussion of the advantages and limitations of this new method, emphasizing its potential to address challenges in optimization within complex systems.

title: High-Dimensional Probability Distributions: An Adaptive Reinforcement Learning Algorithm Based on Microscopic Chaos Theory
abstract: This paper introduces a novel reinforcement learning (RL) algorithm designed to achieve adaptive learning in complex environments. Traditional RL methods often struggle with high-dimensional spaces due to the limitations of sample availability. We propose a new approach that leverages the principles of micro-chaos, specifically its inherent self-organization and sensitivity to initial conditions, to enhance learning efficiency. The core mechanism involves associating the reward function with the microscopic structure of the environment, facilitating a more robust and adaptable learning process. This method overcomes the sample complexity bottleneck of traditional RL, offering potential for more efficient exploration and generalization. The algorithm's design emphasizes the integration of micro-chaos into the learning framework, resulting in behavior strategies tailored to the dynamic and unpredictable nature of the environment. This work presents a framework for adaptive learning in high-dimensional spaces, driven by the principles of micro-chaos.

title: Quantum Feature Selection in Quantum Machine Learning
abstract: This paper investigates the critical role of feature selection within the burgeoning field of quantum machine learning. We propose a novel quantum feature selection algorithm designed to leverage the unique properties of quantum information to identify the most relevant features for a given machine learning task. The core idea is to reduce computational complexity and enhance model accuracy by strategically selecting a subset of quantum features. This approach addresses a significant gap in existing quantum machine learning research, which often overlooks the importance of feature engineering and selection. The proposed algorithm utilizes principles of quantum superposition and entanglement to evaluate feature relevance, ultimately leading to a more efficient and potentially more accurate quantum model. The theoretical framework presented here lays the groundwork for future research and development in this exciting area.

title: Title: Information-Based Constraint Satisfaction – The Quantum Constraint Field
abstract: This paper investigates a novel approach to constraint satisfaction problems, leveraging quantum entanglement to achieve optimal solutions without explicit computation. Traditional methods, often reliant on exhaustive search or complex optimization algorithms, are computationally expensive and struggle with complex problems. We propose a 'Quantum Constraint Field' – a quantum state representing constraints – that enables efficient exploration of the solution space, potentially offering a significant advancement over existing techniques. The core mechanism involves encoding constraints within a quantum state and using entanglement to facilitate rapid, probabilistic solution exploration. This work explores the theoretical foundations and potential practical applications of this quantum constraint field, aiming to identify a paradigm shift in how constraint satisfaction problems are addressed. The paper presents a detailed conceptual framework and outlines a preliminary investigation into the feasibility of using entanglement for efficient constraint satisfaction.

title: Based on Quantum Entanglement Key Agreement Protocol
abstract: This paper presents a novel key agreement protocol leveraging the principles of quantum entanglement. The protocol, termed the "Quantum Entanglement Key Agreement Protocol" (QEKAP), aims to establish a shared secret key between two parties, Alice and Bob, without relying on classical communication channels for key exchange. The core of the protocol utilizes entangled photon pairs to generate correlated random keys, followed by the application of quantum error correction codes to mitigate the effects of noise and ensure accurate key transmission. We demonstrate the feasibility of this approach and highlight its potential advantages over traditional key exchange methods, specifically addressing vulnerabilities associated with eavesdropping and man-in-the-middle attacks. The protocol's security rests on the fundamental laws of quantum mechanics, namely the no-cloning theorem and the uncertainty principle. The key parameters influencing the protocol's performance, such as entanglement fidelity and the overhead introduced by the quantum error correction scheme, are analyzed. Simulation results indicate that QEKAP provides a robust and secure solution for key distribution in quantum networks.

The key parameters influencing the protocol's performance, such as entanglement fidelity and the overhead introduced by the quantum error correction scheme, are analyzed. Simulation results indicate that QEKAP provides a robust and secure solution for key distribution in quantum networks.

title: The Quantum Algorithmic Optimization of Self-Organized Structures
abstract: This paper investigates the application of self-organized quantum algorithms to optimize complex geometric structures. Traditional quantum algorithms are often limited by the inherent challenges of quantum systems, particularly in maintaining coherence and entanglement. This work proposes a novel approach that leverages the dynamic nature of graphs to guide the optimization process, enabling global optimization of complex geometries. The core mechanism centers around the design of a self-organizing quantum algorithm that adapts to the structure of the problem, iteratively refining the solution towards the desired outcome. The research explores the potential of using graph representations to model the geometric structure, and the resulting algorithm's ability to enhance the performance of various optimization tasks. The paper introduces a framework for evaluating the effectiveness of such algorithms using a defined metric. Finally, the work discusses the theoretical implications and potential future directions of this approach.

abstract: This paper introduces a novel framework for machine learning model optimization based on topological structure. The core idea is to leverage the inherent topology of the model's parameters to enhance both model performance and generalization ability. We propose a method that dynamically adjusts the model's structure to promote robustness and reduce overfitting. This approach contrasts with traditional optimization techniques which often rely on local adjustments. The study demonstrates the effectiveness of this method through a series of experiments comparing it to established optimization strategies. The results indicate significant improvements in model accuracy and robustness, particularly in complex datasets.

title: ## The Nautilus-Inspired Adaptive Search Algorithm (NASAL)
abstract: This paper introduces the Nautilus-Inspired Adaptive Search Algorithm (NASAL), a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior and shell morphology of the Nautilus shell. The algorithm leverages the Nautilus's ability to maintain a stable position while adapting its path to navigate complex environments, mirroring a strategy of exploring diverse solutions while retaining promising ones. NASAL incorporates elements of both adaptive step size control, mimicking the Nautilus's subtle movements, and a dynamic neighborhood structure, reflecting the shell's layered design. The core of NASAL lies in a novel 'Spiral-Adaptive Exploration' mechanism that dynamically adjusts the exploration-exploitation balance, and a 'Shell-Based Cluster' strategy for solution representation and diversification. This paper outlines the algorithm's theoretical foundation, detailed implementation, and discusses its potential applications in various optimization problems.

title: Quantum-Enhanced Bayesian Inference for Complex Systems Simulation
abstract: Quantum-Enhanced Bayesian Inference (QEBI) presents a novel approach to complex systems simulation, aiming to significantly improve model accuracy through the application of quantum mechanics in Bayesian inference. This paper introduces a new algorithm, the 'Quantum-Guided Bayesian Network' (QGBN), designed to overcome the computational limitations inherent in traditional Bayesian methods when dealing with highly complex systems. QEBI leverages quantum mechanics to enhance probabilistic inference, reducing computational cost while maintaining high accuracy. The QGBN employs a quantum-guided process that minimizes the influence of noise and allows for more precise uncertainty quantification. We demonstrate its effectiveness through simulations of a dynamic, multi-layered system exhibiting complex interactions and sensitivity to initial conditions. The results show substantial improvements in model accuracy and reduced computational time compared to existing methods.

title: Quantum Sensing Based on Quantum Noise
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to quantum sensing that fundamentally shifts the perspective on quantum noise. Instead of viewing it as an unwanted disturbance, we argue that quantum noise is a critical resource for extracting subtle environmental information. The core concept involves designing a quantum sensor that leverages the statistical properties of quantum noise to precisely measure and interpret its distribution, ultimately enabling the detection of extremely weak signals. This approach moves beyond traditional quantum sensing methodologies which often rely on minimizing noise. We present a theoretical framework and mathematical formalism for this concept, outlining the principles of operation and potential performance characteristics. The underlying mechanism hinges on the ability to correlate the statistical fluctuations of quantum noise with the underlying environmental signal. This work represents a significant departure from conventional thinking and offers a new paradigm for quantum sensing technology. ---

title: Ansell's Epauletted Fruit Bat: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by Foraging Behavior
abstract: This paper presents a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed "Ansell's Epauletted Fruit Bat Algorithm" (AEFBA), inspired by the foraging behavior of *Ansellus noctivagus*, the epauletted fruit bat. These bats exhibit a complex and efficient foraging strategy characterized by a unique 'epauletting' behavior – strategically positioning themselves to maximize their access to food sources. We model this behavior as a multi-dimensional optimization problem and translate it into a new algorithm that combines elements of Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Artificial Bee Colony (ABC). AEFBA utilizes a dynamic 'epaulet' assignment mechanism, where each particle (representing a potential solution) dynamically adjusts its position based on the relative food availability (fitness) of neighboring particles. The algorithm incorporates a 'social influence' factor, mimicking the bats' tendency to follow the most successful foragers. The performance of AEFBA is evaluated on a range of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness and adaptability. The algorithm's key features, including the dynamic epaulet assignment and social influence, are detailed, and its convergence characteristics are analyzed. Results indicate that AEFBA provides a competitive solution to several challenging optimization problems, demonstrating the potential of biomimicry in algorithm design.

title: Information-Theoretic Limits of Deep Learning Representation Learning
abstract: This work investigates the potential information-theoretic limits of deep learning representation learning. It proposes a framework utilizing concepts from information theory – entropy, mutual information, and Kolmogorov complexity – to quantitatively assess information loss throughout the deep learning process, from initial feature extraction to final representation learning. The core argument is that current deep learning architectures may be approaching fundamental limitations as dictated by information theory, specifically concerning the irreducible complexity of data. The research identifies critical thresholds where excessive information loss compromises model performance, suggesting avenues for designing more efficient and robust architectures or altering training strategies to minimize this loss. This approach offers a rigorous, information-theoretic foundation for evaluating deep learning models and potentially guiding future research directions.

title: Angolan Long-Eared Bat Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm for Complex Optimization Problems
abstract: This paper introduces a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed the "Bat Echo Algorithm" (BEA), inspired by the foraging behavior of the Angolan long-eared bat (Plecotus Tanzaniensis). These bats utilize a unique echolocation strategy, adjusting their flight paths based on the reflected echoes to efficiently locate food sources in complex environments. The BEA leverages this adaptation process by employing a population of 'bats' exploring a search space. Each bat's movement is governed by a dynamic adjustment of its echo intensity, proportional to the reflected signal strength. The algorithm incorporates parameters mimicking the bat's behaviour, such as an echo intensity, a frequency, and a flight angle, to guide the search process. Specifically, the algorithm uses the following key equations: * Position Update: $x_{i+1}^k = x_i^k + \alpha_k \Delta x_i^k$, where $x_i^k$ is the position of the *i*-th bat at iteration *k*, $\alpha_k$ is the learning factor, and $\Delta x_i^k$ is the step size determined by the echo intensity. * Echo Intensity Update: $I_{i+1}^k = I_i^k + \beta_k (I_i^k - I_{best}^k)$, where $I_i^k$ is the echo intensity of the *i*-th bat at iteration *k*, $I_{best}^k$ is the maximum echo intensity found so far, and $\beta_k$ is the echo adjustment factor. * Frequency Adjustment: $f_{i+1}^k = f_i^k + \gamma_k (f_i^k - f_{avg}^k)$, where $f_i^k$ is the frequency of the *i*-th bat at iteration *k*, $f_{avg}^k$ is the average frequency of the population, and $\gamma_k$ is the frequency adjustment factor. * Fitness Evaluation: $Fitness(x_i^k) = -\sum_{j=1}^{N} |x_i^k - x^*_j|$, where $x_i^k$ is the position of the *i*-th bat, $x^*_j$ represents the best solution found so far, and *N* is the number of solutions. The BEA exhibits promising performance in solving a range of complex optimization problems, including continuous optimization, combinatorial optimization, and function optimization. The algorithm's parameters are tuned to optimize its convergence rate and solution quality. The results demonstrate the BEA's effectiveness compared to established metaheuristic algorithms such as the Genetic Algorithm and Particle Swarm Optimization.

title: Explainable AI for Deep Reinforcement Learning via Counterfactual Reasoning
abstract: Deep reinforcement learning (DRL) models have demonstrated remarkable success in solving complex tasks, but their inherent complexity often leads to a lack of interpretability. These models are frequently referred to as "black boxes," making it challenging to understand the rationale behind their decisions. This paper proposes a novel approach to explain DRL models by leveraging counterfactual reasoning. We introduce a framework that generates counterfactual examples – "what if" scenarios – by systematically altering the input state and observing the resulting changes in the agent's actions. These counterfactual examples reveal the critical factors driving the agent's behavior, offering a more transparent and understandable explanation of the DRL model's decision-making process. The core of our method relies on identifying the minimal changes in the input that lead to a change in the agent's policy. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through theoretical analysis and discuss its potential applications in various DRL domains. Our approach offers a pathway towards building more trustworthy and reliable DRL systems.

title: ## Blackspot Rhineland Codon Polarized Adaptive Search (BRCPAS) Algorithm
abstract: The blackspot rhineland codon ( *Lophiomusmus manetti*) exhibits remarkable adaptability to changing environmental conditions, particularly in its ability to dynamically adjust its bioluminescence patterns – a process often referred to as "codon polarization". This paper introduces the Blackspot Rhineland Codon Polarized Adaptive Search (BRCPAS) algorithm, a novel metaheuristic optimization technique inspired by this unique biological behavior. BRCPAS utilizes a polarization mechanism, analogous to the codon's light modulation, to selectively explore and exploit the search space. The algorithm maintains a population of potential solutions, each associated with a 'polarization vector' representing its dominance in a given region. The polarization vectors are iteratively adjusted based on the objective function value and the diversity of the population, promoting both convergence and exploration. This paper details the algorithm's core principles, mathematical formulation, and potential applications, highlighting its adaptive nature and suitability for complex optimization problems.

abstract: This paper investigates the application of Quantum Adaptive Algorithms (QAA) to Graph Neural Networks (GNNs). We propose a novel QAGAN architecture that leverages quantum self-optimization to enhance the training and inference process of GNNs. The core of this approach is a dynamically adjusted parameter set derived from quantum self-adaptation, allowing the network to effectively handle complex graph structures. We explore the benefits of this method, focusing on improved performance and robustness compared to traditional GNN algorithms. The proposed QAGAN offers a promising pathway towards more efficient and scalable GNN applications across diverse domains.

title: Quantum State-Based Distributed Time Travel Algorithm (QSTTA)
abstract: This paper investigates the feasibility of a distributed time travel algorithm leveraging quantum state manipulation. The core concept revolves around simulating quantum time travel through precise control of quantum states, utilizing quantum entanglement and quantum gates. We propose a novel approach to time travel that transcends conventional theoretical models, offering potential for accurate temporal manipulation. This research explores the theoretical foundations and practical implications of this algorithm, focusing on the core mechanism of state transformation and the role of quantum entanglement. The goal is to present a mathematically rigorous framework for time travel simulation, addressing key challenges related to accuracy and control. The potential impact of this algorithm extends beyond theoretical exploration, suggesting a paradigm shift in our understanding of time and its manipulation.

title: ## American Lion: A Novel Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm Inspired by the American Lion
abstract: This paper presents American Lion, a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the hunting behavior of the American lion (Panthera leo atrox). The algorithm leverages the lion's strategic movement, hunting tactics, and social dynamics to create a robust and efficient search process. American Lion incorporates key features such as a dynamic territory exploration, a sophisticated decision-making mechanism based on relative fitness, and a social interaction component simulating the lion's collaborative hunting. The algorithm utilizes a population-based approach, with each individual representing a potential solution. The core mechanics are defined by the following: a territory representation, a movement strategy based on fitness gradient, a decision-making rule for territory selection, and a social interaction mechanism for collaborative exploration. The performance of American Lion is evaluated through a series of benchmark functions, demonstrating its effectiveness in achieving global optimization. The algorithm is compared against established metaheuristic algorithms such as Genetic Algorithm (GA) and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) to showcase its advantages in terms of convergence speed and solution quality. The results demonstrate that American Lion provides a competitive and promising approach to tackling complex optimization problems.

title: Quantum Entanglement Complex Geometry Turing Machine
abstract: This paper explores the potential of quantum entanglement to revolutionize the design and analysis of complex geometric Turing machines. Traditional Turing machines rely heavily on explicit algorithm design, while the inherent properties of quantum entanglement offer a fundamentally different approach to simulating complex geometric patterns and behaviors. We propose a novel architecture leveraging entanglement to model geometric intuition more accurately, ultimately enabling the precise characterization of geometric Turing machine behavior. The core mechanism centers around encoding geometric information within entangled states, allowing for dynamic and nuanced geometric simulations. This work introduces a new framework for geometric Turing machine design, demonstrating the potential for significantly enhanced computational power and a deeper understanding of geometric computation.

title: 基于多模态数据融合的异常检测算法
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to anomaly detection leveraging the fusion of multi-modal data. Traditional anomaly detection methods often rely on single data modalities, which can be susceptible to noise and limited in their ability to capture complex patterns indicative of anomalies. This research posits that integrating information from multiple sources – such as text, images, and audio – provides a more robust and accurate representation of the underlying system. The core mechanism involves a fusion technique that combines these disparate data streams, followed by an anomaly detection algorithm applied to the fused data. The resulting system demonstrates improved performance compared to single-modal approaches, particularly in scenarios with noisy or incomplete data. We present a framework for multi-modal fusion and anomaly detection, focusing on algorithmic design and performance evaluation. The proposed method aims to enhance the accuracy and robustness of anomaly detection systems across various applications.

title: ## Afroalpine Vlei Rat: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by Collective Foraging Behavior
abstract: This paper presents a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed the "Vlei Rat Algorithm" (VRA), inspired by the collective foraging behavior of the Afroalpine Vlei Rat ( *Acomys subsp. vlei* ). These rats exhibit remarkable efficiency in locating and exploiting sparse food resources in challenging environments. The VRA leverages this observed behavior, specifically the dynamic adjustments in search strategies and the emphasis on local exploitation, to create a robust optimization algorithm. The algorithm incorporates a novel adaptive population management technique, termed "Patch Switching," and a refined exploitation phase based on a weighted sum of local search distances. We demonstrate the effectiveness of the VRA through simulations on a variety of benchmark optimization problems, including the Rastrigin function, the Sphere function, and the Powell's test functions. Results show that the VRA consistently outperforms several established metaheuristic algorithms, such as the Genetic Algorithm (GA) and the Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO), in terms of convergence speed and solution quality. The key contributions of this work lie in the innovative application of collective foraging strategies to design a metaheuristic algorithm and the demonstration of its superior performance across diverse optimization landscapes.

Manatees exhibit a unique strategy for locating food sources, characterized by a combination of exploration and exploitation. The MSA leverages these behaviors to generate a new optimization algorithm designed for tackling complex, non-linear optimization problems. title: 基于动态拓扑结构的量子计算验证
abstract: Quantum computing offers the potential for revolutionary computational capabilities, but its practical realization faces significant challenges, particularly in algorithm validation. Traditional verification methods often rely on classical algorithms and proofs, which struggle to capture the inherent complexities of quantum systems. This paper introduces a novel quantum algorithm verification technique based on dynamic topology, leveraging self-adaptive learning to dynamically adjust the quantum system's topology to ensure correctness and stability. We propose a mechanism that utilizes a continuous evolution of the system's geometry, allowing for a more precise and flexible validation process. This approach directly addresses the limitations of current methods, offering a promising pathway towards robust quantum algorithms. The paper details the theoretical framework, implementation of the self-adaptive learning algorithm, and preliminary experimental results demonstrating the efficacy of the proposed technique.

title: African Hammada Jerboa: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Behavioral Traits of a Desert Rodent
abstract: This paper presents a novel metaheuristic algorithm, African Hammada Jerboa (AHJ), inspired by the foraging behavior of African Hammada Jerboas, small rodents adapted to the harsh desert environment. These animals exhibit remarkable strategies for resource acquisition, including intermittent movement, clustered searching, and adaptive adjustment based on environmental feedback. AHJ leverages these observed traits to develop a new optimization algorithm suitable for complex, non-linear problems. The algorithm incorporates a clustered search mechanism, a dynamic adjustment of step sizes proportional to resource availability, and a novel 'inertia modulation' technique mimicking the jerboa's response to sand dune shifts. The performance of AHJ is evaluated across a range of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating competitive results compared to established metaheuristic algorithms such as Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Simulated Annealing (SA). The key innovations of AHJ lie in its adaptive exploration and exploitation strategies, leading to improved convergence rates and solution quality. The algorithm's design principles are discussed in detail, and future research directions are proposed.

title: Cost-Sensitive TSK for Recognition of Imbalanced Epilepsy EEG Signal
abstract: Epilepsy EEG signal recognition is an important method for epilepsy detection. However, the traditional machine learning methods used for epilepsy EEG signal recognition face many challenges. For example, traditional intelligent recognition methods often ignore the imbalance of epilepsy EEG signals, which misclassifies positive samples and may cause serious consequences; the existing imbalanced classification methods ignore class-guided global inter-class correlations among samples, resulting in poor classification results. In order to overcome these challenges, a cost-sensitive-based TSK method (CITSK) is proposed for imbalanced epilepsy EEG signal recognition. This proposed method constructs a Class-guided Sample Collaborative Relationship (SCR) matrix to assign higher weight to positive minority samples, and supplements global inter-class collaborative penalty information on the basis of the traditional static cost-sensitive matrix. Then, a model combining the SCR matrix and TSK is proposed, which inherits the good generalization ability and interpretability of TSK while ensuring classification performance. Experiments on real EEG datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method and its applicability to the imbalanced classification of epileptic EEG signals. Quantitatively, the CITSK method achieves an average Accuracy of 93.96%, an average F_measure of 88.33%, and an average G_means of 91.34% across various imbalanced datasets. Furthermore, comparative evaluations demonstrate that the proposed CITSK achieves superior overall performance across comprehensive evaluation metrics compared to baseline models, offering a highly robust and interpretable solution for imbalanced data scenarios via reasonable global inter-class penalty compensation.

abstract: The article presents an analysis of rules for collisionless substitution in Transparent Procedural Logic, a new version of Transparent Intensional Logic.The article compares rules for collisionless substitution in Transparent Procedural Logic and the current standard form of Transparent Intensional Logic.The article shows that, in some cases, the current rule for collisionless substitution into double execution in Transparent Procedural Logic creates problems in determining the object v-constructed by the resulting construction.

title: Uso de grafos direcionados ponderados aplicados na criptografia RSA
abstract: A Teoria dos Grafos oferece diversas aplicações na computação, inclusive na segurança da informação. Este trabalho propõe uma abordagem alternativa para a criptografia RSA, utilizando caminhos entre dois vértices de digrafos ponderados com números primos como peso. Em vez de gerar novos primos a cada criação de chaves, como no Multiprime RSA, a proposta utiliza um grafo previamente construído, onde os pesos são atribuídos com base no algoritmo de geração de primos em um intervalo, entre a e b, de Ezz-Eldien et al., que apresenta complexidade de tempo O(b) e espacial O(b-a). Apesar do custo inicial elevado devido à construção do grafo, a geração subsequente de chaves torna-se mais eficiente. A solução mantém a possibilidade de grande quantidade de chaves possíveis que serem criadas do Multiprime RSA, porém aumentando a robustez do sistema e permite paralelismo na cifração e decifração. No entanto, como as variantes do RSA tradicional, continua vulnerável à computação quântica.

title: Reinforcement Learning for Symbolic Equation Solving
abstract: We present a reinforcement-learning agent that solves symbolic equations step by step, covering both nonlinear closed equations (radicals, exponentials, trigonometric) and a controlled class of restricted-open families requiring a change of variables (CoV) such as completing the square. We cast algebra as an MDP with a dynamic action space and a tree-structured policy (TreeMLP). The main policy learns from reward alone with no supervised solution traces; the CoV substitution comes from a supervised generator interchangeable with a CAS call. On closed equations the agent matches the prior best on CommonCore (0.93 greedy vs. ConPoLe's 0.925) under a single policy. On four hand-designed restricted-open families (quadratic, cubic, quartic, exponential) it reaches 0.79 beam / 0.67 greedy, exceeding the strongest non-learned search (A-star, 0.64). Learned CoV timing has content only on the exponential family, the one requiring a nested CoV, where a natural rule solves none of the held-out equations while the policy solves 75% from reward alone. At 10x scale a sharp seed-level bimodality emerges; a UCB learning-progress curriculum shows a non-significant positive trend toward mitigating it. We do not claim general open-equation solving: every open-equation result is confined to these four controlled families.

title: Theory of Quantum-Enhanced Interferometry with General Markovian Light Sources
abstract: Quantum optical systems comprising quantum emitters interacting with engineered optical modes generate non-classical states of light that can be used as resource states for quantum-enhanced interferometry. However, outside of well-controlled systems producing either single-mode states (e.g. Fock states or squeezed states) or highly symmetric multi-mode states (e.g. superradiant states), their potential for quantum advantage remains uncharacterized. In this work, we develop a framework to analyze quantum enhanced interferometry with general Markovian quantum light sources. First, by connecting the quantum Fisher information (QFI) of the photons emitted by a source to the multi-time correlation functions and the source dynamics, we elucidate the link between the level structure and spectrum of the source to a potential quantum advantage in interferometry. Second, we analyze optimal measurement protocols that can be used to achieve this quantum advantage with experimentally available optical elements. In particular, we show that tunable optical elements with Kerr non-linearity can always be harnessed to implement the optimal measurement for any given source. Simultaneously, we also outline general conditions under which linear optics and photodetection is enough to implement the optimal measurement.

title: EKSTRAKSI KONTRIBUSI DALAM PAPER AKADEMIK MENGGUNAKAN ALGORITMA T5 DAN INTEGRASI BERT–T5
abstract: Pesatnya Perkembangan publikasi ilmiah menimbulkan tantangan dalam proses peninjauan literatur, khususnya dalam mengidentifikasi kontribusi utama yang disampaikan oleh suatu paper akademik. Kontribusi penelitian merupakan elemen penting karena mencerminkan fokus penelitian, metode yang diusulkan, serta temuan utama yang menjadi nilai kebaruan suatu karya ilmiah. Namun, perbedaan struktur dan gaya penulisan menyebabkan proses identifikasi kontribusi secara manual menjadi tidak efisien. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk mengembangkan sistem ekstraksi kontribusi paper akademik secara otomatis menggunakan pendekatan berbasis Natural Language Processing. Penelitian ini menerapkan model Text-To-Text Transfer Transformer (T5) dan model hibrida BERT+T5, dengan BERT berperan sebagai encoder kontekstual sebelum proses generasi ringkasan oleh T5. Dataset yang digunakan terdiri dari paper akademik bidang ilmu komputer yang dianotasi secara manual. Penandaan kalimat kontribusi dilakukan berdasarkan indikator yang diacu dari literatur, yaitu kalimat yang menyatakan fokus atau tujuan penelitian, metode atau pendekatan yang diusulkan, serta hasil atau temuan utama, yang umumnya muncul pada bagian abstrak, pendahuluan, dan hasil paper. Evaluasi kinerja sistem dilakukan menggunakan metrik ROUGE-1 F, ROUGE-2 F, dan ROUGE-L F untuk menilai kesesuaian leksikal, serta BERTScore F1 untuk mengukur kesamaan semantik. Hasil pengujian menunjukkan bahwa model T5 memiliki keterbatasan dalam mengekstraksi kontribusi secara akurat, yang tercermin dari nilai ROUGE yang rendah. Sebaliknya, model BERT+T5 menunjukkan peningkatan performa yang signifikan pada seluruh metrik evaluasi. Temuan ini menunjukkan bahwa integrasi BERT mampu meningkatkan pemahaman konteks kalimat akademik, sehingga sistem lebih efektif dalam mengidentifikasi dan mengekstraksi kalimat yang merepresentasikan kontribusi utama penelitian.

title: A Federated Deep Learning Framework for Privacy-Preserving Digital Identity Anomaly Detection in Distributed Networks
abstract: The increasing use of distributed digital services has created significant challenges in detecting identity anomalies while protecting sensitive user information. This study develops a federated deep learning framework for privacy-preserving digital identity anomaly detection in distributed networks. The research focuses on decentralized learning, where identity-related data remain within participating client environments, and only model parameters are exchanged for collaborative training. The methodology includes data preprocessing, local deep learning, federated parameter aggregation, privacy protection, anomaly classification, and performance evaluation. The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed approach achieves 98.76% accuracy, 98.42% precision, 98.61% recall, and 98.51% F1-score. The federated training analysis further shows progressive improvement across communication rounds, reaching 97.68% validation accuracy and a 98.21% detection rate. These findings indicate that federated deep learning can effectively support distributed identity anomaly detection while reducing direct exposure of sensitive identity data. The framework provides a foundation for secure and scalable identity analytics in networked environments.

title: STROMATIC PHILOSOPHY of Quantum Computing
abstract: The future that is sketched is not that of an omniscient machine nor of a simple acceleration of what is already known. It is that of a new capacity to generate knowledge about regimes of nature and mathematics that until now remained opaque. That capacity will be fully realized only to the extent that the operative subject continues to weave, with material rigor, conceptual ambition, and historial responsibility, the threads that make possible the passage from the possible to the effective. In that fabric — dense,discontin., co-determined — resides the true philosophical depth of quantum computing.

title: Dynamic Quantum Topology Framework
abstract: Abstract: This paper introduces a novel dynamic quantum topology framework designed to automatically optimize quantum computation performance by dynamically adjusting the quantum system's topology based on computational tasks. Traditional parameter adjustment methods often rely on manual intervention, lacking the inherent topological structure of quantum systems. Our framework leverages this structure to enhance quantum computation efficiency through intelligent adjustments. This research explores the potential of this approach to improve the design and execution of quantum algorithms.

title: Nonlinear Topological Geometry for Quantum Computing Verification
abstract: This paper explores the application of nonlinear topological geometry to quantum computing, focusing on the design of a quantum key distribution (QKD) protocol leveraging quantum entanglement. We propose a novel approach that utilizes the inherent properties of quantum entanglement to establish a mathematically verifiable QKD scheme. The core mechanism involves constructing a quantum state distribution based on entangled topological structures, facilitating rigorous mathematical analysis and theoretical validation of QKD protocols. The paper demonstrates the potential of this technique to simplify the process of validating quantum computations, offering a fundamentally new way to approach the challenges of quantum security.

title: Graph Neural Networks for Knowledge Reasoning and Discovery
abstract: This paper explores the application of Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) to knowledge reasoning and discovery. Traditional knowledge representation and reasoning techniques often struggle with the complexity and interconnectedness of real-world knowledge. This work proposes a novel approach that leverages the power of GNNs to represent and process knowledge in a graph structure. By learning representations of these graphs, GNNs can effectively perform knowledge reasoning tasks such as relation extraction, entity linking, and knowledge graph completion. The core claim is that utilizing GNNs enhances knowledge utilization efficiency. The central mechanism involves translating knowledge into a graph structure and employing GNNs to learn and interpret this structure for inference and discovery. This approach overcomes limitations of traditional methods relying on logical or rule-based reasoning, offering a more nuanced understanding of complex relationships. We demonstrate the potential of GNNs to unlock valuable insights from vast knowledge bases. ---

title: Algorithm Genetic Optimization: An Adaptive Optimizer
abstract: This paper introduces an algorithm genetic optimization (AGO) system designed to automatically adjust optimization parameters based on changes in the optimization target. The core concept of AGO is to frame the optimization process as an evolutionary algorithm, iteratively refining the parameters to converge towards the target solution. We propose a novel approach to parameter adjustment that leverages the inherent adaptability of genetic algorithms, specifically focusing on dynamically adapting the optimization strategy to maintain optimal performance. The system is presented with a detailed explanation of the algorithm's architecture, the mechanism of parameter adjustment, and its potential benefits in various optimization scenarios. This research addresses the limitations of traditional optimization methods by introducing a method capable of adapting to complex, evolving target spaces.

title: Federated Learning with Differential Privacy: Enhancing Privacy in Decentralized Model Training
abstract: Federated learning (FL) presents a promising paradigm for training machine learning models on decentralized data sources without directly exchanging data. However, the inherent collaborative nature of FL still poses privacy risks. This paper investigates the integration of differential privacy (DP) into the FL framework to provide an enhanced level of privacy protection. We introduce a novel approach where noise is injected into model parameters during the training process, adhering to the principles of DP. This mechanism mitigates the risk of information leakage from individual user data while maintaining model accuracy. We formally define the proposed algorithm and analyze its privacy-utility trade-off. The results demonstrate that the incorporation of DP significantly strengthens the privacy guarantees of FL, offering a robust solution for privacy-sensitive applications. Our work contributes to the growing body of research focused on secure and privacy-preserving FL techniques.

title: Semantic Graph Embeddings for Knowledge Graph Completion via Graph Transformers
abstract: Knowledge graphs (KGs) are increasingly utilized for various applications, including question answering, recommendation systems, and drug discovery. A central challenge in KG management is knowledge graph completion, which involves predicting missing relationships between entities within the graph. Traditional methods for KG embedding often struggle to capture the complex, structural relationships inherent in KGs. This paper proposes a novel approach leveraging Graph Transformers to learn powerful semantic embeddings for KGs and effectively tackle the knowledge graph completion problem. We utilize a transformer architecture, specifically designed for graph data, to model the interactions between nodes and edges. The attention mechanism within the transformer enables the system to learn contextualized embeddings that capture intricate relationships within the graph, ultimately leading to improved accuracy in predicting missing links. Our experiments demonstrate the efficacy of this approach, showcasing its ability to outperform existing methods on benchmark datasets.

title: Dynamic Quantum Circuit Synthesis and Optimization
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to quantum circuit synthesis and optimization, addressing the significant challenges in designing efficient quantum algorithms. The core idea is to develop a system capable of dynamically generating and optimizing quantum circuits based on the specific characteristics of quantum hardware and the demands of the targeted quantum algorithm. The system employs optimization algorithms, such as quantum annealing or genetic algorithms, to navigate the vast space of possible quantum circuits, incorporating hardware constraints throughout the optimization process. This automated design approach aims to overcome the complexities inherent in traditional quantum circuit synthesis, ultimately accelerating the progress of quantum computing by facilitating the realization of practical and efficient quantum algorithms. The developed system is designed to adapt to varying quantum hardware limitations, leading to optimized circuit designs for a wide range of quantum algorithms. The key contribution lies in the integration of hardware-aware optimization within a dynamic synthesis framework.

title: Adaptive Non-Linear Encryption (ANEC)
abstract: This paper introduces Adaptive Non-Linear Encryption (ANEC), a novel cryptographic protocol leveraging the principles of quantum entanglement and stochastic noise to achieve enhanced security in key exchange and data transmission. The core design centers on a dynamically adjustable quantum entanglement mechanism, which introduces inherent unpredictability into the encryption process. This unpredictability significantly mitigates the risk of cryptanalysis by making it exponentially more difficult for adversaries to break the encryption. The paper details the design, implementation, and security analysis of ANEC, emphasizing its potential for robust and adaptable security. The focus is on presenting a robust and mathematically-grounded protocol that addresses limitations of existing cryptographic methods.

title: Explainable Deep Learning Models Based on Causal Reasoning
abstract: This paper investigates the problem of interpretability in deep learning models, often referred to as the "black box" problem. Current methods for explaining deep learning decisions frequently lack a fundamental understanding of *why* a model makes a particular prediction. We propose a novel approach that integrates deep learning models with causal reasoning techniques to achieve a more robust and meaningful explanation of model behavior. Specifically, we aim to identify causal relationships within the model's learned representations and use these relationships to elucidate the reasons behind its predictions. This framework allows us to move beyond simply highlighting features that contribute to a prediction (as in methods like LIME or SHAP) and instead focus on the underlying causal mechanisms driving the model's decision-making process. The core idea is to treat the deep learning model as a complex, potentially biased, causal system and leverage established causal inference techniques to analyze and interpret its behavior. We demonstrate the feasibility and potential of this approach, highlighting its advantages in terms of transparency and trust.

title: Decentralized Learning with Federated Graph Neural Networks
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to decentralized learning utilizing Federated Graph Neural Networks (FedGNNs). The core idea is to facilitate collaborative knowledge discovery across a network of devices by employing locally maintained graph representations and periodically synchronized Graph Neural Networks (GNNs). This framework addresses the limitations of traditional federated learning, particularly when dealing with graph-structured data, where raw data sharing poses significant privacy concerns. The system avoids direct data exchange by allowing devices to collaboratively learn through the exchange of model updates, preserving data privacy while enabling effective knowledge transfer. The proposed FedGNN architecture consists of local graphs and locally trained GNNs, synchronized via a novel aggregation mechanism. We demonstrate the feasibility and effectiveness of this approach through a theoretical analysis and outline the key components required for implementation. The system is designed to be scalable and adaptable to various decentralized network topologies. This work represents a significant step towards privacy-preserving collaborative learning in complex, graph-based environments.

abstract: This paper investigates the synergistic integration of high-dimensional space self-adaptation algorithms and machine learning techniques to enhance the generalization and efficiency of machine learning models. This approach fosters robust models capable of handling complex datasets and achieving superior generalization. title: Barbastelle: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by Barbastelle Bats
abstract: This paper presents Barbastelle, a new metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of Barbastelle bats. Barbastelle combines elements of Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Artificial Bee Colony (ABC) with a novel adaptive adjustment mechanism mimicking the bats' echolocation and flight patterns. The algorithm utilizes a dynamic population size, velocity updates based on both global and local best positions, and a 'pulse-echo' strategy for exploring the search space. Performance evaluations on a range of benchmark optimization problems demonstrate that Barbastelle exhibits competitive convergence rates and solution quality compared to established metaheuristic algorithms. The key innovation lies in its ability to dynamically adapt the exploration and exploitation phases based on the perceived complexity and density of the search landscape, mirroring the bats' efficient use of limited information. The algorithm's parameters are designed to be easily tunable, allowing for flexible adaptation to different problem characteristics. This research contributes a novel optimization approach with potential applications in diverse fields including engineering design, financial modeling, and machine learning.

title: ## Banahaw Forest Mouse-Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm for Complex Optimization Problems
abstract: This paper presents a novel metaheuristic algorithm, the Banahaw Forest Mouse-Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm (BFM-MHA), designed to address complex optimization challenges. The algorithm's inspiration stems from the remarkable navigation skills and adaptive foraging behaviors of the Banahaw Forest Mouse, a small rodent inhabiting the mountainous regions of the Philippines. BFM-MHA leverages principles of spatial awareness, risk assessment, and resource allocation observed in these mice to generate a robust and efficient search process. The core of the algorithm involves a multi-dimensional representation of the search space, a stochastic movement strategy mimicking the mouse's exploratory gait, and a dynamic risk evaluation mechanism based on simulated environmental hazards. Mathematical formulations are presented to detail the algorithm's key components, including the position update rule, the risk assessment function, and the convergence criterion. The algorithm is demonstrated through simulations on several benchmark optimization problems, showcasing its ability to achieve competitive solutions and exhibit superior performance compared to established metaheuristic methods like Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Simulated Annealing (SA). The efficacy of BFM-MHA is evaluated based on solution quality, computational efficiency, and robustness across a range of problem landscapes. title: Quantum Entanglement-Driven Distributed Collaborative Learning
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to distributed collaborative learning leveraging the unique properties of quantum entanglement. This approach offers a potential solution to the bandwidth and latency constraints inherent in traditional distributed learning paradigms. We present a theoretical framework outlining the key principles and potential benefits of this method.

Traditional approaches often rely on static, predefined topologies, limiting the algorithm's adaptability to data variations. This work proposes a novel algorithm that dynamically adjusts topological parameters based on data distribution, enabling more effective geometric modeling and numerical simulation. We detail the core mechanism, including the iterative adjustment of parameters and the resulting benefits in terms of model fidelity and simulation accuracy. The algorithm's effectiveness is demonstrated through a series of illustrative examples, showcasing its capacity to handle complex data distributions and achieve superior results compared to traditional methods.

title: Complex System Modeling and Control based on Multi-Agent Collaboration
abstract: This paper investigates the application of multi-agent collaboration for the modeling and control of complex systems. Traditional methods often struggle with the inherent complexity, non-linearity, and dynamic nature of these systems. We propose a novel approach that leverages a collection of intelligent agents working together to represent and manipulate the system's behavior. The core idea is to decompose the complex system into manageable sub-systems, each embodied as an agent, allowing for localized control and emergent global behavior through collaborative communication and interaction. We explore the mathematical framework underpinning this approach, focusing on agent interaction models, communication protocols, and control strategies. The significance of this method lies in its adaptability to systems with evolving structures and its potential to overcome the limitations of centralized control methods. We present a theoretical foundation and explore key considerations for successful implementation, demonstrating its effectiveness in addressing complex system challenges.

title: ## Butterfly Inspired Adaptive Exploration and Exploitation Algorithm (BIEEA)
abstract: This paper introduces the Butterfly Inspired Adaptive Exploration and Exploitation Algorithm (BIEEA), a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of Monarch butterflies. The algorithm leverages the butterfly's unique strategies of both exploration (searching for new food sources) and exploitation (returning to previously successful food sources) to navigate complex search spaces. BIEEA incorporates adaptive parameters that dynamically adjust the balance between exploration and exploitation based on the current search state. The core of the algorithm lies in a modified butterfly movement strategy utilizing a combination of Lévy flight and gradient descent, along with an adaptive inertia weight scheme. The algorithm's performance is evaluated theoretically, demonstrating its potential for effective optimization in various problem domains. Key aspects include the butterfly population's position update, the Lévy flight component's scaling factor, and the adaptive inertia weight calculation. The algorithm is designed to be computationally efficient and adaptable to different problem landscapes.
