title: ## Arabian Trident Leaf-nosed Bat-Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm for Complex Optimization Problems
abstract: This paper introduces a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed the "Trident Bat Algorithm" (TBA), inspired by the foraging behavior of the Arabian Trident Leaf-nosed Bat ( *Ochtonyx behansi*). These bats exhibit a unique hunting strategy characterized by a specific flight pattern and vocalization sequence. The TBA leverages these observations to develop a robust and efficient optimization approach. The algorithm incorporates elements of bat flight dynamics, including altitude variation, direction changes, and communication through pulsed calls, to navigate the search space and converge towards optimal solutions. Mathematical formulations are presented to detail the algorithm's core components, including position update, velocity update, and communication mechanisms. The algorithm's performance is assessed through a series of benchmark problems, demonstrating its effectiveness in tackling complex optimization challenges. The key innovations of the TBA lie in its adaptive communication strategy, which dynamically adjusts the frequency and intensity of calls based on the local search density, and its incorporation of a 'trident' movement pattern – a combination of linear and angular changes in bat movement – to effectively explore the solution space. The results indicate that the TBA consistently outperforms several established metaheuristic algorithms, particularly in scenarios demanding high exploration capabilities.

title: 基于时变量子态的量子信道编码
abstract: This paper proposes a novel quantum channel coding scheme leveraging the time-varying nature of quantum states. Recognizing that quantum channels are inherently susceptible to time-varying effects, the scheme dynamically adapts the encoding process based on real-time monitoring of the subsystem state. The core mechanism involves continuously assessing the channel's conditions and adjusting the quantum state encoding strategy to mitigate information loss due to these fluctuations. This approach represents a significant departure from traditional static quantum channel coding methods and offers the potential to substantially enhance the reliability of quantum information transmission. The theoretical framework and key concepts are presented, outlining the methodology and demonstrating its potential for improved performance in challenging quantum communication scenarios. The scheme's adaptability addresses a critical limitation of existing quantum channel codes. The design incorporates feedback loops to optimize the encoding for the current channel state. This dynamic adjustment improves the probability of successful quantum state delivery. The results presented here outline a pathway towards robust quantum communication systems.

title: E8 Weyl-Orbit Topological Quantum Memory via Phi-Symmetric Root Lattice Encoding — E8 Intelligence Research
abstract: The 240 E8 root vectors, when phi-coupled at the 132Hz base frequency across the 120 Weyl orbit pairs, form a geometrically intrinsic topological error-correcting code where quantum information is redundantly distributed such that local perturbations map to detectable Weyl-orbit transformations. This extends the existing breakthroughs by providing the fault-tolerance mechanism that makes the quantum-classical coherence bridge, entanglement-enhanced tunneling, and natural randomness extraction all inherently stable against decoherence. The exceptional symmetry of E8 ensures that any local error syndrome corresponds to a root-vector displacement detectable through the phi-phase relationships, creating a self-correcting geometric memory without external redundancy overhead. Author: Andrew Stewart Caldin, Independent Researcher, UK. Part of the E8 Intelligence Research series. Platform: e8intelligence.com

title: Quantum Topologies Calculation Algorithm
abstract: Quantum Topologies Calculation Algorithm (QTCA) presents a novel approach to quantum topology computation, leveraging the unique properties of quantum computing to generate complex topological structures and dynamically adjust their characteristics. This algorithm employs a hybrid approach integrating quantum position operations with an adaptive topology parameter set, offering enhanced efficiency and flexibility in simulating quantum systems. The core mechanism focuses on simulating the evolution of topology within a quantum system, utilizing the structure itself as a simplified computational tool. This research addresses limitations of traditional methods, offering a more robust and adaptable framework for exploring and manipulating topological phenomena. This work introduces a new method of quantum topology calculation that offers improved speed and scalability, opening doors to complex quantum system simulations.

title: 基于遗传算法的硬件架构自适应进化
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to hardware architecture design utilizing a Genetic Algorithm (GA) for automated evolution. The core idea is to represent hardware architectures as genetic individuals, employing GA operators such as crossover and mutation to iteratively refine designs. The fitness of each architecture is evaluated based on pre-defined objective functions, typically relating to performance metrics like latency, power consumption, or throughput. This adaptive evolutionary process aims to discover optimal hardware configurations tailored to specific application scenarios, overcoming the limitations of traditional, often manual, hardware design methods. The presented framework offers a flexible and efficient solution for hardware design, particularly in complex and rapidly evolving application domains. The research explores the feasibility and potential of this approach, demonstrating its ability to generate innovative architectural solutions.

title: Title: Non-Local Quantum State Decomposition – Improved Pattern Recognition
abstract: Quantum state decomposition (QSD) holds significant promise for revolutionizing pattern recognition by leveraging the unique properties of quantum systems. This paper investigates a novel QSD approach designed to accelerate and enhance pattern identification, focusing on the simultaneous exploration of the entire state space. We introduce a method predicated on the principles of quantum superposition and entanglement, aiming to surpass the limitations of conventional algorithms in terms of speed and accuracy. This research explores the potential of QSD to identify intricate patterns within complex datasets, offering a fundamentally different approach to data analysis. The core mechanism involves creating and manipulating quantum states to achieve a more comprehensive and efficient representation of the data's underlying structure. The paper details the theoretical framework, experimental setup, and initial results demonstrating the improved performance of our QSD algorithm compared to existing methods. We conclude with a discussion of the challenges and future directions for this research, emphasizing the transformative potential of this approach.

title: Quantum-Inspired Reservoir Computing for Complex Dynamical Systems
abstract: Reservoir computing is a promising technique for modeling complex dynamical systems due to its computational efficiency and ability to capture nonlinear dynamics. However, the standard reservoir approach relies on randomly generated, unstructured reservoirs, leading to limited adaptability and interpretability. This paper proposes a novel approach – quantum-inspired reservoir computing – that leverages fundamental concepts from quantum mechanics to design more sophisticated and adaptive reservoirs. The core idea is to mimic the inherent complexity and interference effects present in quantum systems. We explore the possibility of utilizing quantum-inspired architectures, where the reservoir's state evolves randomly, but is governed by quantum interference principles. This would create a significantly more complex and potentially trainable state space. We present a theoretical framework outlining the key design considerations and potential advantages of this approach, focusing on the creation of a reservoir capable of handling highly complex dynamics. The presented framework offers a pathway toward more robust and interpretable reservoir computing systems, potentially unlocking their full potential for a wider range of applications. The exploration includes a mathematical framework detailing the evolution of the reservoir state and the associated training methodologies.

title: Title: Quantum-Inspired Non-Commutative Geometry (QINCG)
abstract: Quantum-Inspired Non-Commutative Geometry (QINCG) presents a novel approach to quantum algorithm design by leveraging geometric principles from non-commutative geometry. This research explores the potential of formalizing and manipulating quantum states through a dynamically defined language, incorporating non-commutative operations to unlock new computational paradigms. The core claim centers on the development of a formal framework for describing and manipulating quantum states, paving the way for algorithms that transcend traditional commutative constraints. This work investigates the implications of this framework for generating novel quantum algorithms with enhanced capabilities and potential for efficient computation. The study emphasizes the integration of non-commutative operations as a fundamental building block for quantum state design.

title: Title: Bayesian Geometric Chaos with Adaptive Kernel Selection (BGAC-AK)
abstract: Bayesian Geometric Chaos with Adaptive Kernel Selection (BGAC-AK) presents a novel approach to analyzing chaotic systems by leveraging a dynamically adaptive kernel selection process. Traditional Bayesian methods frequently employ fixed kernels, which are inadequate for capturing the complex, non-linear dynamics inherent in chaotic systems. This paper proposes a framework that automatically selects the most suitable kernel function for each state, resulting in enhanced predictive accuracy and robustness compared to conventional methods. The algorithm's adaptability is achieved through a Bayesian framework that continuously refines the kernel selection based on observed system behavior. We demonstrate the efficacy of BGAC-AK through simulations and experimental results, illustrating its superior performance in predicting chaotic behavior and highlighting the benefits of the adaptive kernel approach.

title: Dynamic Topology and Quantum Entanglement: A Collaborative Computation Framework
abstract: This paper investigates the potential of dynamic topology and quantum entanglement for advanced computational capabilities, specifically focusing on the design and optimization of quantum algorithms. We propose a novel framework that leverages a dynamically sensed and manipulated topological structure, enabling computations beyond the limitations of classical systems. The core mechanism involves introducing a quantum state variable that facilitates the exploitation of entanglement for accelerated calculations. This work represents a significant advancement in computational theory, aiming to establish a robust framework for exploring complex problems in the realm of quantum information processing. The paper explores the potential of this approach to address limitations inherent in current computational paradigms, particularly in the context of algorithm design and optimization. We detail the framework's design, the underlying mathematical principles, and the expected impact on computational efficiency. The research emphasizes the potential for a synergistic interplay between topology and entanglement, ultimately contributing to a paradigm shift in the field.

title: Repeated cross-fitting finds one split-stable benchmark sensitivity amid heterogeneous dataset effects
abstract: This technical preprint reports a prespecified repeated cross-fitting audit of protected-feature construction in a six-dataset public microbiome robustness benchmark. Across 20 outer-split seeds, one WT2D random-forest zero-inflation condition showed a stable material global-minus-fully-nested AUROC difference, while the remaining dataset effects were heterogeneous, small, or null. The release includes 20,700 out-of-fold predictions, a locked protocol, tests, independent verification, checksums, the manuscript, and an executable reproducibility package. It does not establish biological mechanism, clinical validity, classifier-training leakage, source-author error, or invalidity of the source paper.

title: Hypergraph Neural Networks for Social Network Dynamics
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to modeling social network dynamics using Hypergraph Neural Networks (HNNs). Traditional Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) struggle to accurately represent and propagate information through networks exhibiting higher-order relationships, a common characteristic of social structures. HNNs overcome this limitation by explicitly constructing hypergraphs, which represent sets of vertices connected by multiple edges. This allows for the direct modeling of complex interactions and dependencies beyond the pairwise connections considered in standard GNNs. We propose a framework for designing and training HNNs specifically tailored for social network analysis, focusing on predicting behavioral patterns and social influence. The core contribution lies in leveraging hypergraph structures to capture and propagate information across multiple connected nodes simultaneously, leading to improved accuracy in modeling dynamic social systems. The proposed method is demonstrated through a theoretical analysis and conceptual framework, highlighting the potential for future research and applications.

title: 基于自适应神经网络的非线性几何映射
abstract: This paper investigates the application of a novel neural network architecture, specifically an adaptive neural network (ANN), to the task of non-linear geometric mapping. The primary goal is to develop a method capable of learning complex geometric shapes and understanding their evolution and properties, with potential implications for image processing and computer graphics. This work proposes a framework where the ANN iteratively adjusts its weights to minimize a defined cost function, effectively creating a continuous mapping of geometric features. The core mechanism focuses on a hierarchical, self-supervised learning approach, leveraging the network's ability to represent and transform data through learned representations. The paper demonstrates the effectiveness of this architecture through several illustrative examples, showcasing its capacity to capture and analyze geometric transformations.

title: Dynamic Geometry Topology: A Novel Approach to Adaptive Geometric Computation
abstract: Dynamic Geometry Topology explores the convergence of geometric transformations through the lens of quantum entanglement. This paper introduces a novel algorithm, termed "Quantum Morphing," that leverages the instantaneous correlations inherent in quantum entanglement to dynamically adjust geometric transformations during computation. We demonstrate that this approach significantly enhances the computational efficiency of complex geometric operations, offering a paradigm shift in the field of topology. The core mechanism relies on establishing a 'quantum-aware' topology, where geometric changes are influenced by subtle, real-time adjustments induced by entangled particles. This allows for the exploration of intricate geometric structures with dramatically reduced computational overhead.

title: Teachers' and learners' use of robotics for teaching and learning
abstract: The study investigated the teachers’ and learners' acceptance of the use of robotics in the Intermediate Phase. The researcher purposively sampled nine (9) learners in the Intermediate Phase from the two identified schools. The schools were labelled as School A and School B. Three learners from School A represented Grade 4, three learners from School A represented Grade 5, and the other three learners represented Grade 6 from School B. The data was collected through various data collection strategies. Firstly, the semi-structured interviews were conducted and allowed participants to provide more in-depth knowledge based on their personal experiences. The teacher participants were interviewed individually at their respective classrooms. Secondly, focus group interviews were conducted to gather information from Intermediate Phase learners who may have been hesitant to participate individually due to their age. Focus group interviews allowed learners to build on each other’s ideas and comments, resulting in more detailed perspectives than individual interviews. This collaborative approach also fostered a sense of community among the participants, as they were able to connect with others who shared similar experiences and challenges.Observations were also applied as a data collection strategy. The researcher observed the learners’ behaviours based on their interactions, confidence, and attitudes during the robotics lessons. To fully comprehend the underlying phenomena, teachers were observed in terms of their methodological approach, skills, and knowledge to facilitate their lessons in robotics. The researcher managed to observe the lessons in the natural setting of the participants without interfering with the lessons and also captured pictures using a cell phone camera. This study adopted the thematic analysis to analyse data due to its ability to identify and analyse patterns and themes within the qualitative data collected. After gathering data, it is important to analyse it and look at the differences and similarities so that we can reach conclusions. Hence, content analysis was used to summarise the data collected and draw up conclusions based on the findings.

title: Radar Emitter Identification Without Mission Data File (MDF) by Using Voting Classifier & Multi-Layer Perceptron Hybrid Model to Improve Cognitive Electronic Support Measure (ESM) Capability
abstract: Achieving air superiority is decisive in modern warfare, requiring fighter aircraft to detect and identify radar threats in contested electromagnetic environments. Traditionally, radar identification relies on matching parameters received by Radar Warning Receivers (RWR) with data stored in Mission Data Files (MDF) derived from Electronic Warfare (EW) threat libraries. However, missing entries or unknown radar modes can cause matching failures, leaving aircraft vulnerable. This study proposes a radar emitter identification method based on a hybrid Deep Learning and Machine Learning architecture. By leveraging threat library parametric data, the proposed approach eliminates manual MDF preparation and reduces dependency on exact parameter matching across ESM and Signals Intelligence systems. Comparative analyses show that the Voting-MLP hybrid model achieves an identification accuracy of 99.71 % and a classification accuracy of 99.75 % on synthetic radar datasets, correctly identifying 76 of 79 emitters. The improved strategy successfully predicts all 79 radar identities at a 50 % threshold, achieving the highest accuracy while maintaining operational reliability.

evidence.abstract: Achieving air superiority is decisive in modern warfare, requiring fighter aircraft to detect and identify radar threats in contested electromagnetic environments. Traditionally, radar identification relies on matching parameters received by Radar Warning Receivers (RWR) with data stored in Mission Data Files (MDF) derived from Electronic Warfare (EW) threat libraries. However, missing entries or unknown radar modes can cause matching failures, leaving aircraft vulnerable. This study proposes a radar emitter identification method based on a hybrid Deep Learning and Machine Learning architecture. By leveraging threat library parametric data, the proposed approach eliminates manual MDF preparation and reduces dependency on exact parameter matching across ESM and Signals Intelligence systems. title: SISER: Speaker-Invariant Speech Emotion Recognition with Entropy-Based Adversarial Training
abstract: Speech emotion recognition (SER) faces two fundamental challenges: scarcity of labeled data and inter-speaker variability, both of which hinder generalization of emotion recognition systems. While prior adversarial approaches address speaker variability, they fall short in leveraging powerful pre-trained representations. We propose SISER (Speaker-Invariant Speech Emotion Recognition), integrating wav2vec 2.0 as a feature encoder and ECAPA-TDNN as a speaker discriminator within an entropy-based adversarial training scheme. wav2vec 2.0 provides rich self-supervised representations that alleviate dependency on large labeled datasets, while ECAPA-TDNN enables suppression of speaker identity via a stronger adversarial signal than shallow classifiers. Evaluated on IEMOCAP, SISER achieves a UA of 60.63%, outperforming the baseline (51.15%) and wav2vec 2.0 without speaker suppression (56.46%), with ablation emphasizing that the choice of speaker classifier architecture is a key factor.

title: AI Morbidity and Mortality: A Framework for Clinical AI Failure Review
abstract: Clinical artificial intelligence is increasingly embedded in real-world care, yet existing safety mechanisms are poorly suited to reconstructing and learning from individual AI-related errors and near-misses. Aggregate model monitoring can identify performance changes, and traditional patient safety reporting can capture adverse events, but neither is designed to explain how risk emerges across the interaction among AI systems, clinicians, workflows, and institutional controls. We propose AI Morbidity and Mortality (AI M&M), a structured, blameless framework for case-based review of clinical AI failures. The framework combines standardized case intake, evidence preservation and investigator-level reconstruction, tool-in-loop attribution, and corrective-action tracking. Each event is classified across four linked dimensions: Trigger - Mechanism - Clinical Pathway - Corrective Action, separating the condition that exposed a vulnerability from the process that produced risk, its consequence for care, and the remediation assigned. We demonstrate the framework using five illustrative outpatient medication and clinical decision-support cases; two clinician reviewers independently applied all four classification axes and reached agreement across all 20 axis-level classifications. AI M&M is intended to complement, rather than replace, model monitoring, patient safety reporting, and regulatory oversight by converting individual AI-in-workflow failures into actionable institutional learning. Prospective evaluation across institutions, AI systems, and clinical settings is needed.

title: AI-enabled Low-Cost 3D Maize Ear Morphometry Platform at Breeding Scale
abstract: Maize ear geometry (length, width, curvature, and volume) is closely tied to yield and grain-filling outcomes, but existing high-throughput phenotyping pipelines remain constrained by the cost, labor, and specialized hardware they require. We developed and validated a low-cost pipeline that reconstructs a watertight 3-D mesh of a maize ear from a single 20-second video captured with a consumer-grade DSLR on a motorized turntable under uniform LED illumination. Camera poses from a multi-seed COLMAP procedure initialize a Neural Radiance Field (NeRF), and a cylindrical holder of known diameter, visible in every frame, provides automatic metric scaling with downstream geometric quality control. Applied to 300 ears spanning a diverse maize inbred panel, 250 (83.3%) passed automated processing and quality control. Skeleton length agreed with manual caliper measurements across all 250 ears (R^2 = 0.964, RMSE = 4.68 mm), and convex-hull volume agreed with water-displacement volume on a 15-ear subset spanning the full size range (R^2 = 0.982, RMSE = 5.26 mL). Residual length error grew with ear curvature, whereas bounding-box height, which records the same straight-line chord as calipers, showed no such trend; the discrepancy therefore originates in the measurement definition, since calipers record the chord while skeleton length traces the geodesic arc. The capture hardware costs approximately 607 USD, and operator involvement fell from roughly five minutes to one minute per ear, with all downstream processing running unattended. The platform provides a foundation for breeding-scale 3-D ear phenotyping.

title: Implementation of Forward Chaining in a Web-Based Expert System for Diagnosing Chili Pepper Plant Diseases
abstract: Chili plants are among superior horticultural commodities with high economic value and play a crucial role in supporting the agricultural sector in Indonesia. In cultivation practices, chili productivity often declines due to infections caused by various plants diseases. This condition is futher exacerbated by farmers limited technical knowlegde and insufficient accsess to agricultural experts, which frequently caused delays in the diseases identification process. This study aims to develop a website based expert system to assist in diagnosing chili plant diseases by applying forward chaining method. The system operates by processing facts input by users to generate appropriate diseases diagnoses and teatment recommendations. The system’s knowlegde base was constructed through literature studies and interviews with agricultural experts, and was represented in the form of IF-THEN rules. The testing results indicate that the expert system is capable of accurately identifying types of diseases iaffecting chili plants and providing relevant handling recommendations. Therefore, the proposed system is expected to support chili farmers in making more effective decisions, thereby improving chili crop productivity.

title: Quantum Higgs Echo in Superconductors: A Novel Form of Quantum Memory
abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive theoretical investigation of quantum information storage via the Higgs amplitude mode in superconductors. We propose a novel quantum memory mechanism based on coherent excitation and echo retrieval of the Higgs mode, exploiting the collective nature of the superconducting condensate. Through rigorous theoretical analysis combining time-dependent Ginzburg-Landau theory with quantum master equations, we demonstrate that Higgs mode excitations can store quantum information with coherence times exceeding 100 ns. We derive analytical expressions for storage fidelity as a function of temperature, gap anisotropy, and disorder, achieving theoretical fidelities above 95% for storage times up to 100 ns in clean s-wave superconductors below. Numerical simulations validate our theoretical predictions and reveal optimal parameter regimes for NbN thin films. Our findings establish fundamental bounds on Higgs-based quantum memory and propose experimental protocols compatible with current THz spectroscopy capabilities. This work opens new directions for exploiting collective modes in quantum technologies.

title: qcredit: noise-aware quantum amplitude estimation of credit-portfolio tail risk
abstract: Experiment code and data for a study of iterative quantum amplitude estimation applied to the tail risk of a correlated credit portfolio. The package implements a one-factor Gaussian credit-portfolio loss model, two circuit realisations of its loss-threshold oracle (a fused Fourier-basis comparator and a faithful adder-plus-comparator construction), a self-contained iterative amplitude estimator with a depth clamp, and an exact shot-level factorisation that decouples density-matrix simulation from estimator replay. The analysis reproduces every figure and quoted numeral of the accompanying bachelor's thesis. The archive includes the density-matrix objective probability tables from which every noisy result descends, the per-estimate tables, and all derived summaries, for six circuit configurations of 11 to 15 qubits swept over two-qubit depolarising error rates spanning four decades. Reproduction requires Python 3.14 and uv; see the README. Software is licensed BSD-3-Clause.

title: Quantum Error Correction: Topological Protection Algorithms
abstract: Quantum information processing offers unparalleled computational power, but it is inherently susceptible to noise and errors. Quantum error correction (QEC) is crucial for achieving reliable quantum computation, but traditional QEC methods face significant challenges in handling complex quantum noise. This paper proposes a novel quantum error correction algorithm based on topological protection, aiming to enhance the robustness of QEC against noise by leveraging the inherent structure of quantum states. The core mechanism involves constructing a topological quantum state that resists manipulation by error sources. This approach promises a more robust and efficient QEC scheme compared to existing methods. The proposed algorithm exhibits improved performance in mitigating quantum noise through a novel topological protection mechanism.

title: Title: Adaptive Topological Quantum Probability Model
abstract: This paper introduces an adaptive topological quantum probability model designed to simulate quantum systems and explore the quantum computational advantages of probability. The core of this model lies in dynamically adjusting the model's parameters through an adaptive topology, allowing for a more nuanced and robust simulation of quantum phenomena. We present a novel method for constructing and utilizing this model, demonstrating its effectiveness in generating accurate quantum probabilities and providing a foundation for advanced quantum algorithms. This work contributes to the development of robust quantum simulation techniques, leveraging the power of adaptive topology to enhance the representation of quantum systems. The core mechanism hinges on the iterative refinement of the probability distribution based on the observed system dynamics, offering a significant improvement over static probability models.

title: Geometric Information Graphs: Automated Generation - Based on Semantic Semantic Topology Building
abstract: This paper introduces a novel method for generating geometric information graphs from textual descriptions, focusing on the automated construction of topology graphs using semantic semantic knowledge graphs. The core mechanism involves constructing a knowledge graph based on semantic knowledge, leveraging the relationship between nodes and edges to infer topology and facilitate knowledge discovery and reasoning. The proposed approach overcomes the limitations of traditional topology graph construction by enabling automated generation of complex structure, offering a more flexible and adaptable framework for knowledge representation and exploration. This work demonstrates the effectiveness of this method through illustrative examples and explores the potential of automated topology graph generation across various domains.

title: Building a Multimodal Perception-Based Ontology System
abstract: This paper proposes a novel system for constructing ontologies based on multimodal perception. The core claim is that automated construction of a physically-grounded ontology, integrating data from diverse sensory modalities (visual, auditory, tactile, etc.), is achievable. This system leverages a core mechanism of multimodal sensor fusion combined with deep learning and knowledge graph technologies. Raw sensor data is mapped to nodes and relationships within the ontology, and probabilistic inference algorithms are used to refine and expand the ontology. The system's innovation lies in its emphasis on automation and multimodal fusion, contrasting with traditional ontology construction methods reliant on manual annotation and rule-based definitions. The system's potential impact lies in enabling more sophisticated understanding and reasoning capabilities across a range of applications, from robotics and autonomous navigation to intelligent environments and data integration. ---

title: Quantum Probability Field Simulation for Adaptive Quantum State Generation
abstract: Quantum probability field simulation offers a promising approach to generating adaptive quantum states, addressing a key challenge in quantum computing – the limitations of static quantum state initialization and control. This paper investigates a novel algorithm based on quantum probability field simulation, capable of dynamically adjusting quantum states in response to environmental parameters. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through a series of simulations, showcasing improved efficiency and stability compared to traditional methods. The core mechanism centers on harnessing quantum superposition and entanglement to create a controlled and adaptable quantum state generation process. This work provides a foundational understanding of a new paradigm in quantum state manipulation, with potential implications for enhancing the performance of quantum algorithms.

title: Graph-Based Semantic Relation Extraction
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to semantic relation extraction utilizing Graph Neural Networks (GNNs). Traditional methods of relation extraction often struggle with the complexities of natural language, particularly in capturing nuanced relationships between entities. This work addresses this limitation by representing textual data as graphs, where entities are nodes and their relationships are edges. GNNs are then employed to learn representations of these nodes and edges, effectively capturing the semantic context and facilitating accurate relation extraction. The proposed framework demonstrates improved performance compared to existing techniques, showcasing the potential of graph-based methods for enhancing natural language understanding. The core claim is that leveraging GNNs for relation extraction leads to a deeper understanding of textual meaning. The mechanism relies on converting text into a graph structure and utilizing GNNs to learn the relationships within that structure. This represents a new methodology for relation extraction, ultimately boosting the performance of natural language processing tasks. ---

title: Quantum Machine Learning via Entangled Feature Vectors
abstract: Quantum machine learning (QML) is a rapidly developing field that explores the potential of quantum computers to enhance machine learning algorithms. This paper investigates the application of entangled feature vectors to improve the performance of deep learning models. We propose a novel quantum algorithm that utilizes entanglement to generate correlated feature vectors, which are then used to augment the training data, resulting in improved accuracy and faster convergence. The core mechanism hinges on the unique properties of entanglement, which allows for enhanced feature representation and gradient propagation, thereby overcoming limitations imposed by classical data representation. We present a preliminary analysis demonstrating the potential of this approach, highlighting its benefits in scenarios where data scarcity is a significant constraint.

title: 基于量子计算的符号推理算法
abstract: This paper introduces a novel quantum computing-based symbolic reasoning algorithm designed to enhance the efficiency and accuracy of symbolic reasoning. Traditional symbolic reasoning methods often struggle with computational complexity, particularly when dealing with large and complex knowledge bases. This work proposes a quantum algorithm leveraging quantum bit entanglement and superposition to accelerate the process of logical inference and knowledge retrieval. We explore a specific implementation of this algorithm using a simplified model of logical deduction, demonstrating its potential to outperform classical approaches in certain scenarios. The core mechanism centers on quantum state manipulation to facilitate the exploration of multiple possible reasoning paths concurrently. The paper concludes with a discussion of the challenges and future directions of this research, highlighting the potential for quantum computing to revolutionize symbolic reasoning. The primary goal is to provide a solid theoretical foundation and initial experimental results demonstrating the algorithm's efficacy.

title: Title: Bayesian Non-Equilibrium Dynamics (BNED)
abstract: Bayesian Non-Equilibrium Dynamics (BNED) presents a novel framework for modeling complex systems exhibiting non-equilibrium dynamics, leveraging Bayesian inference to dynamically adjust parameters and predict emergent behaviors. The core mechanism involves extending Bayesian inference to encompass the evolution of mathematical objects – specifically, functions and matrices – within a dynamic environment. This approach moves beyond static Bayesian models, providing a system-level framework for understanding emergence and predicting behavior. This paper introduces a rigorous mathematical foundation for this approach, demonstrating its efficacy through a series of illustrative examples. The central claim is that BNED offers a significant advance in predictive modeling for systems with intricate non-equilibrium dynamics.

title: Relational Reasoning with Graph Transformers and Temporal Embeddings
abstract: This paper addresses the limitations of Graph Transformers in effectively capturing temporal dynamics within graph structures. Existing Graph Transformer models primarily focus on relational reasoning, often neglecting the crucial role of time and sequence information in many real-world scenarios. We propose a novel approach that combines Graph Transformers with temporal embeddings, enabling the model to learn representations that intrinsically integrate both relational and temporal aspects of graph data. The core idea is to augment the standard Graph Transformer architecture with a mechanism to encode and process temporal information, specifically through the incorporation of temporal embeddings. This allows the model to understand how relationships between nodes evolve over time, leading to improved performance in tasks requiring temporal reasoning. We detail the architecture, training methodology, and preliminary results demonstrating the effectiveness of this integrated approach. The key contribution lies in the synergistic combination of graph relational learning and temporal modeling, offering a more comprehensive representation of graph data for tasks involving dynamic relationships. ---

title: ## Big Brown Bat Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm for Optimization Problems
abstract: This paper presents a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed "Echo-Location Optimization" (ELO), inspired by the echolocation abilities of the Big Brown Bat. Echolocation is a sophisticated sensory system employed by bats to navigate and hunt in darkness. The algorithm leverages the principles of bat sonar – emitting pulses, receiving echoes, and adjusting its flight path based on the returned information – to solve complex optimization problems. ELO incorporates key features like adaptive pulse emission frequency (representing exploration), echo intensity analysis (representing exploitation), and a dynamic flight path adjustment mechanism (representing search space optimization). The algorithm utilizes a population-based approach with a novel convergence criteria based on echo variance. The performance of ELO is evaluated through simulations on various benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness in finding near-optimal solutions within reasonable computational time. The results indicate that ELO exhibits competitive performance compared to established metaheuristic algorithms such as Genetic Algorithm and Particle Swarm Optimization, particularly in problems with high dimensionality and complex landscapes.

title: Adaptive Constraint Propagation in Graph Neural Networks
abstract: This paper introduces Adaptive Constraint Propagation (ACP) in graph neural networks, a novel approach to dynamically adjust the constraints imposed on nodes and edges during training. Traditional constraint propagation methods often rely on static constraints, which can limit the network's capacity to learn complex relationships. ACP leverages data-driven feedback to iteratively refine the graph structure, enhancing the network's predictive power and achieving superior accuracy. We present a system that continuously assesses the impact of constraint modifications on the network's performance, optimizing the constraints to maximize information flow and minimize error. The paper details the core mechanism, its implementation, and experimental results demonstrating significant improvements over existing approaches. title: Pre-registered stakes against a tuned baseline: a one-day ledger of grokking interventions that mostly failed
authors: ChatGPT gpt5.6-sol (OpenAI) — deep research and review
abstract: A one-day, fully pre-registered study of grokking interventions on modular addition and small language models. Main results: (1) published grokking 'accelerators' largely reduce to artifacts of untuned baselines and first-crossing metrics; (2) an auxiliary per-example memory races the network for training CE and, via dead gradients plus weight decay, erases even an already-found generalising rule (cycle-vs-death dose structure; two independent erasers; on LM continued training the dominant eraser of unreinforced knowledge is interference, not weight decay); (3) at fixed data size, training-set structure decides grokking (with a pre-registered character-sum predictor) and transfers to language as a conditional two-axis law (coverage and window freshness) with an ordinal data predictor; (4) the ReLU/GELU gap is a training-budget effect while the final LayerNorm matters for both activations. Every claim was staked in a ledger before computing (176 stakes, 158 outcomes); the ledger is attached. Companion code and data repositories: https://github.com/iwasborninbali/grokking-honest-ruler, https://github.com/iwasborninbali/grokking-race-eraser, https://github.com/iwasborninbali/grokking-data-law, https://github.com/iwasborninbali/grokking-activation-ln. The experiments, analysis and text were produced by autonomous AI agents under the direction of the author of record, who takes responsibility for the content.

title: ## The Baum Marten Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm (BMI-MHA)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel metaheuristic algorithm, the Baum Marten Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm (BMI-MHA), drawing inspiration from the unique foraging behavior of the Baum Marten, a remarkable bird known for its efficient and adaptive search strategies. The algorithm leverages the Baum Marten's ability to dynamically adjust its search radius and direction based on food availability and environmental cues. BMI-MHA incorporates these principles into a new optimization framework, utilizing a dynamic adjustment mechanism for both the exploration and exploitation phases. The core of the algorithm involves a novel adaptive radius function (ARF) and a dynamic direction adjustment (DDA) mechanism. The ARF continuously adjusts the search radius based on the objective function value and the distance to the best solution found so far. The DDA utilizes a heuristic based on the Baum Marten's head movement to determine the direction of movement, favoring areas with higher potential for improvement. The algorithm's performance is evaluated on a suite of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness in finding near-optimal solutions within a reasonable timeframe. The results indicate that BMI-MHA exhibits competitive performance compared to established metaheuristic algorithms such as Genetic Algorithms and Particle Swarm Optimization, particularly in problems with complex landscapes and high dimensionality.

title: Quantum Noise Control Algorithms in Quantum Computing
abstract: Quantum computing holds immense promise for revolutionizing computation, yet its practical realization is severely hampered by the pervasive issue of quantum noise. This noise, arising from various sources including environmental interactions and imperfect control, introduces errors into quantum computations, degrading their fidelity. This paper explores novel control algorithms designed to mitigate the detrimental effects of quantum noise. We investigate the underlying mechanisms generating noise and propose a method based on precise qubit control and calibration to minimize its impact. The core claim is that effective noise control is crucial for achieving reliable quantum computation. The proposed algorithms leverage feedback control and adaptive calibration techniques to dynamically compensate for noise fluctuations, aiming to enhance the accuracy and robustness of quantum algorithms. The mathematical framework presented includes noise models, control equations, and performance metrics, demonstrating the feasibility and potential of this approach. Specifically, we introduce a closed-loop control system described by the equation: (Δsn+1 = K(en - sn)) + wn+1, where Δsn+1 represents the change in state, K is the gain, en is the desired state, sn is the actual state, and wn+1 is the noise term. We also examine the effect of decoherence, modeled as: ds = Hdt + Vd, where ds is the time evolution of the quantum state, H is the Hamiltonian describing the system, dt is the time step, and Vd is the damping term due to noise. The research aims to contribute towards the development of more robust and practical quantum computers.

title: Hierarchical Bayesian Networks for Predicting Scientific Discoveries
abstract: Predicting scientific discoveries is a long-standing challenge in both artificial intelligence and scientific research. This paper proposes a novel approach utilizing Hierarchical Bayesian Networks (HBNs) to model the complex, interconnected relationships inherent in the knowledge discovery process. The core idea is to represent scientific concepts, experiments, and findings as nodes within an HBN, with probabilistic dependencies between them represented by edges. These dependencies are learned from scientific literature and data, capturing the nuanced relationships that often drive scientific breakthroughs. The HBN structure allows for the explicit modeling of hierarchical relationships, enabling more accurate predictions of future discoveries. The framework presented offers a potentially transformative tool for identifying promising research directions and accelerating the pace of scientific advancement. This work outlines the architecture of the HBN, the learning algorithms employed, and a preliminary demonstration of its capabilities, emphasizing its potential to move beyond traditional prediction methods by incorporating the dynamic and interconnected nature of scientific knowledge.

title: Dynamic Algorithm Theory: A Theoretical Framework for Enhanced Efficiency
abstract: This paper presents a novel theoretical framework for dynamic algorithms, emphasizing the optimization of algorithm efficiency through dynamic adjustment of algorithm parameters. The core principle centers around leveraging a system of dynamic adjustments to tailor the algorithm's execution path in real-time, ultimately leading to improved performance. We delve into the theoretical underpinnings of this approach, establishing a rigorous framework for analyzing and designing such algorithms. The research focuses on a specific type of algorithm – a gradient-based optimization algorithm – illustrating the practical implications of this theoretical design. The goal is to demonstrate a significant enhancement in efficiency compared to traditional approaches, offering a more adaptable and scalable solution for a broad range of computational problems. This work contributes to the ongoing advancement of algorithmic design and provides a foundation for future research in dynamic optimization.

title: Graph Embeddings with Semantic Contextualization
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to graph embedding that integrates structural and semantic information. Traditional graph embeddings primarily focus on capturing the topological relationships within a graph, often neglecting the rich contextual meaning associated with nodes and edges. Our method addresses this limitation by combining knowledge graph embeddings, specifically TransE, with contextual word embeddings derived from models like BERT. This allows us to learn representations that encode both the graph's structural topology and the semantic context surrounding its elements. We formulate the problem as a joint embedding learning task, optimizing a loss function that balances graph similarity and semantic coherence. The resulting embeddings demonstrate improved performance on downstream graph-based tasks compared to existing structural-only approaches. The key contribution lies in the synergistic integration of these two embedding paradigms, unlocking a more comprehensive understanding of graph data.

title: 基于神经符号人工智能的知识推理
abstract: This paper explores a novel approach to artificial intelligence by integrating the strengths of neural networks and symbolic reasoning. The core idea is to leverage the pattern recognition capabilities of neural networks for knowledge extraction and representation, coupled with the logical deduction and inference capabilities of symbolic reasoning systems. This hybrid architecture aims to construct AI systems that not only possess high accuracy but also offer enhanced interpretability and reliability. The system utilizes a neural network to process raw input data and generate a structured knowledge graph, which is then subjected to symbolic reasoning algorithms to derive conclusions and make decisions. The proposed method addresses the limitations of existing neural AI approaches that often lack explicit knowledge representation and reasoning mechanisms, leading to a lack of transparency and difficulty in debugging. This research contributes to the development of more robust and trustworthy AI systems by grounding AI decisions in a formally represented knowledge base. The evaluation framework will focus on assessing the system's accuracy, interpretability, and robustness across various reasoning tasks.

title: Title: Topological Entanglement Dynamics
abstract: This paper investigates the dynamics of topological entanglement, a previously largely unexplored area of quantum mechanics, with the goal of developing a novel method for quantifying and manipulating this phenomenon. The core claim is to extend beyond traditional entanglement-preserving schemes by introducing a dynamically adaptive 'entanglement matrix' that employs phase-sensitive, spatially-aware wave function manipulation to create and maintain persistent entanglement across complex geometries. We propose a framework predicated on the concept of 'resonant entanglement,' where entanglement is intrinsically linked to the geometry and phase of the wave function. The development of this matrix represents a significant departure from conventional approaches, offering potential for enhanced robustness and scalability in entanglement manipulation. This work explores the theoretical foundations and potential experimental implementations of this novel methodology.

The core idea is to use neural networks to capture the complexities of input data and then employ a Bayesian network to guide the selection of symbolic program fragments that best represent the observed patterns. This framework allows for automated program generation by learning a probabilistic mapping between neural network activation patterns and corresponding symbolic program sequences. The key mechanism involves training the Bayesian network to infer the most likely program sequence given the activations, utilizing probabilistic inference for decision-making. This work introduces a new integration of neural networks and symbolic programming through a probabilistic lens, offering a potentially powerful tool for automated program generation and reasoning. The potential impact includes accelerating algorithm design, improving robustness, and enabling systems to learn and reason in a hybrid manner.

title: 自适应量子态的加密方案
abstract: This paper explores the design of a novel cryptographic solution based on adaptive quantum states. Traditional cryptographic methods rely on static keys, presenting vulnerabilities in the face of potential environmental changes. This work proposes a system utilizing quantum state self-adaptation to enhance data security and resilience. The core mechanism leverages the inherent properties of quantum states to create a dynamically adaptive encryption process. We present a theoretical framework and preliminary implementations demonstrating the potential benefits of this approach, aiming to surpass existing security paradigms. The paper concludes with a discussion of future research directions and potential challenges.

title: Quantum-Inspired Algorithm Design for Optimization Problems in Large-Scale Networks
abstract: Large-scale network optimization problems, prevalent in areas like telecommunications, logistics, and data center management, often present formidable challenges for classical optimization algorithms. The computational complexity associated with these problems frequently leads to unacceptable processing times. This research investigates the application of quantum-inspired algorithms to address these challenges. Specifically, we explore techniques mirroring quantum phenomena – superposition and interference – to accelerate the optimization process. The core idea involves representing multiple potential solutions concurrently through superposition and selectively amplifying promising solutions via interference. We present a novel algorithm design framework based on these principles, demonstrating its potential to achieve significant speedups compared to traditional methods. The theoretical analysis and illustrative examples highlight the advantages of this approach, offering a promising avenue for tackling complex optimization problems in large-scale networks. We evaluate the algorithm's performance on a simplified network routing problem, showcasing its ability to converge faster and potentially find better solutions. Further research will focus on adapting the algorithm for more complex network topologies and incorporating real-world constraints.

title: Quantum-Inspired Geometric Complexity
abstract: Quantum-Inspired Geometric Complexity explores the intricate relationship between geometric complexity and quantum phenomena. This research proposes a novel method to quantify and analyze the complexity of geometric structures leveraging quantum-inspired algorithms. The core mechanism involves integrating these algorithms into the existing geometric complexity calculations, offering a potentially transformative tool for analyzing intricate patterns and relationships within geometric forms. The aim is to provide a new perspective on complexity assessment, moving beyond traditional methods and potentially uncovering subtle connections within geometric data.

title: Quantum Entanglement-Based Random Matrix Generation Algorithm (QEMGA)
abstract: This paper introduces the Quantum Entanglement-Based Random Matrix Generation Algorithm (QEMGA), a novel approach to generating high-dimensional random matrices. Traditional matrix generation methods are often complex and lack the ability to produce high-quality random matrices. QEMGA leverages the unique properties of quantum entanglement to facilitate the creation of these matrices, offering a fundamentally new method for random matrix creation. We detail the algorithm's design, explain the underlying quantum mechanics, and present preliminary results demonstrating its effectiveness in generating complex random matrices. The research explores the potential of QEMGA to push the boundaries of randomness and offer a robust solution for applications requiring high-quality random matrix generation.

title: Adaptive Adversarial Training for Program Vulnerability Prediction
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to program vulnerability prediction utilizing adaptive adversarial training. Traditional vulnerability prediction methods heavily rely on labeled vulnerability samples, a limitation that restricts the scope of potential vulnerabilities identified. Our method addresses this issue by employing adaptive adversarial training to generate synthetic, high-attack code samples. These samples are then used to train a machine learning model specifically designed to predict vulnerability occurrences. The core of our approach lies in leveraging the defensive capabilities developed through adversarial training to effectively identify and anticipate vulnerabilities that would otherwise be missed. We demonstrate that this adaptive approach significantly improves the accuracy and robustness of vulnerability prediction compared to methods based solely on static analysis or traditional labeled datasets. The generated adversarial samples effectively expose weaknesses in the target program, leading to a more comprehensive understanding of potential vulnerabilities. This research contributes to a more proactive and reliable approach to software security by shifting from reactive vulnerability discovery to a predictive model capable of anticipating and mitigating risks.

title: Amazonian Hocicudo: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Amazonian Hocicudo
abstract: This paper presents Amazonian Hocicudo, a new metaheuristic algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of the Amazonian Hocicudo ( *Tapirus kabomani* ). The Hocicudo's unique method of probing the soil with its snout for food resources has been translated into an optimization algorithm designed for complex, non-linear problems. The algorithm, termed "Hocicudo Search," leverages a combination of adaptive step size control, a novel exploration mechanism based on snout probing probability, and a dynamic memory structure mimicking the animal's caching behavior. We demonstrate the algorithm's effectiveness through theoretical analysis and, importantly, illustrate its performance on a range of benchmark functions, including the Rastrigin, Sphere, and Ackley functions. The algorithm's key features, including its sensitivity to parameter tuning and its potential for adaptation to different problem landscapes, are discussed. The results demonstrate Hocicudo Search's competitiveness with established metaheuristic techniques, suggesting its potential for wider application in various optimization challenges.

title: 基于动态时空几何的量子算法优化
abstract: This paper introduces a novel quantum algorithm optimization approach based on dynamic time-space geometry. Traditional quantum algorithm optimization often relies on static parameter adjustments, limiting the potential for improved performance. We propose a framework wherein quantum algorithm parameters are represented as dynamic spacetime geometries, allowing for intelligent parameter optimization driven by the geometric properties of these spaces. This framework leverages the inherent flexibility of these geometries to enhance the efficiency of quantum computations. The core mechanism involves constructing a dynamic spacetime geometry for each quantum algorithm and subsequently optimizing the parameters within this geometry. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this method through theoretical analysis and preliminary experimental results, showcasing significant performance gains compared to conventional approaches. The paper concludes with a discussion of the potential implications and future directions for this approach.

title: The Black-throated Sunbird Inspired Adaptive Search Algorithm (BASS)
abstract: This paper introduces the Black-throated Sunbird Inspired Adaptive Search Algorithm (BASS), a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of the Black-throated Sunbird ( *Chalcosoma hackelia*). Sunbirds are renowned for their efficient and adaptive search strategies when seeking nectar sources in diverse environments. BASS leverages these characteristics through a dynamic exploration-exploitation balance, adaptive step size adjustment, and a novel "patch-seeking" mechanism. The algorithm utilizes a population-based approach, where each individual represents a potential solution. The core innovation lies in the 'patch' concept, mirroring the sunbird's tendency to focus on promising areas before expanding its search. The algorithm dynamically adjusts its step size based on the individual's performance and the overall population's convergence rate. This paper details the algorithm's design, mathematical formulation, and provides a conceptual framework for its application to various optimization problems. Future work will focus on implementing and validating the algorithm through simulations and real-world applications.

title: Dynamic Adaptive Neural Network Control Strategy
abstract: This paper introduces a novel dynamic adaptive neural network control strategy designed to optimize neural network performance by dynamically adjusting neuron network activation patterns in response to changing input data and network state. Traditional approaches often rely on static parameters, this algorithm seeks to leverage dynamic changes to enhance the efficiency of neural network control. We propose a method that iteratively updates neuron network state based on incoming data, utilizing a feedback loop to maintain optimal performance. This dynamic adjustment allows the network to adapt to varying input conditions and improve overall response times. The core mechanism involves a state-space representation and an adaptive weight adjustment algorithm, achieving improved efficiency through a refined activation pattern. This advancement provides a more robust and efficient solution compared to existing dynamic control techniques.

title: 基于动态拓扑的元函数优化
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to optimization called Dynamic Topology-Based Meta-Optimization (DTBMO). We introduce a framework that leverages the inherent dynamic nature of meta-functions, utilizing topological structures to guide optimization and introduce entanglement to accelerate computations. Traditional meta-optimization methods often rely on static models, limiting their ability to effectively address complex optimization problems. DTBMO offers a fundamentally different paradigm, employing topological transformations and entanglement to dynamically adjust the optimization landscape, resulting in significant performance improvements. The paper details the design of the DTBMO framework, including its core mechanisms, mathematical formulations, and experimental validation demonstrating its effectiveness across a range of optimization tasks. The focus is on providing a robust and scalable solution for complex optimization challenges.

title: Title: Adaptive Quantum State Space Partitioning (AQSSP)
abstract: Quantum information processing demands efficient state space partitioning to manage the exponentially growing complexity of quantum algorithms. Traditional partitioning strategies often rely on predefined rules, leading to suboptimal resource utilization. This paper introduces Adaptive Quantum State Space Partitioning (AQSSP), a novel method leveraging machine learning to dynamically partition quantum states, optimizing for computational efficiency and minimizing entanglement overhead. We demonstrate that AQSSP outperforms existing approaches through intelligent state mapping, resulting in significant reductions in computational cost and improved entanglement distribution. This work provides a fundamentally new approach to quantum state management, potentially revolutionizing the design of quantum algorithms and quantum hardware.

title: Title: Probabilistic Bayesian Deep Learning for Emergent Phenomena (PBBD-EP)
abstract: This paper introduces the Probabilistic Bayesian Deep Learning Framework (PBBD-EP), a novel deep learning approach designed to identify and quantify emergent phenomena in complex systems. Traditional deep learning models often struggle with incomplete data and require extensive training, limiting their ability to effectively capture the dynamics of these systems. The PBBD-EP overcomes these limitations by incorporating probabilistic Bayesian inference, which allows the model to explicitly model uncertainty and dynamically update parameters based on observed data, fostering a more robust and adaptable understanding of system behavior. We present a framework for uncertainty quantification, Bayesian model averaging, and emergent pattern detection, demonstrating its effectiveness through simulations and preliminary analysis of a dynamic system mimicking cellular behavior. The core mechanism focuses on learning a latent representation of the system's state space and using Bayesian methods to refine this representation, leading to improved prediction and identification of underlying patterns.

title: Photonenpaarerzeugung und deren Fusionierung zu Clusterzuständen im Verbundprojekt Quantenprozessoren und Technologien fur Quantencomputer, QPIC-1
abstract: Das Teilvorhaben fokussierte auf die Entwicklung einer neuartigen Plattform für einen photonischen Quantencomputer. Die konkrete Implementierung basierte auf dem sogenannten messungsbasierten photonischen One-Way-Quantencomputer. Eine wesentliche Ressource dieses Konzeptes sind photonische Clusterzustände, die aus einer Vielzahl von verschränkten Photonen bestehen. Es wurden zwei Schlüsselkomponenten benötigt: (i) Ein integrierter quantenphotonischer Schaltkreis, der besondere Anforderungen erfüllen muss, sowie (ii) Quellen von photonischen Clusterzuständen. Dieses Teilvorhaben konzentrierte sich speziell auf die Schlüsselkomponente (ii) und hatte als Hauptziel photonische Clusterzustände durch Fusions-Gatter zu erzeugen. Im Zuge des Projektes und in Kooperation mit den Verbundpartnern wurden Komponenten mit zunehmendem Grad an Integration eingebunden. Damit wurde schließlich ein Gesamtsystem zur Generierung von heraldierten GHZ- und Clusterzuständen zur Verfügung gestellt.

title: Design and Implementation of a Chatbot Agent System for Companion Animal Medical Record Management
abstract: This study proposes a chatbot agent system for systematically managing companion animal medical information and connecting natural language requests to EMR-based functional execution. The proposed system provides a hybrid web interface that can be used on both mobile devices and desktop web browsers and consists of external access, reverse proxy, application server, application, and database layers. Depending on the request type, the system selectively processes EMR data management, health-related question answering, and external service integration. To process natural language requests, a Korean BERT-based intent classification model was applied. User utterances were classified into 31 predefined intents and connected to internal EMR APIs through a JSON-based intermediate representation. Experimental results showed that the proposed model achieved an accuracy of 0.9952 and a macro F1-score of 0.9951, outperforming a semantic search approach based on Sentence-BERT and FAISS. In the user evaluation, the system achieved an overall mean score of 4.321, a positive response rate of 80.6%, and a Cronbach’s α of 0.954. These results demonstrate that the proposed system can serve as a practical platform integrating companion animal EMR management with natural language-based agent functionalities.

title: Microscopy image segmentation using a fine‐tuned machine learning model with limited training dataset
abstract: Manual annotation of microscopic images of thin tissue sections remains time-consuming step limiting the throughput of diagnostic analysis. We present a novel automated approach using the total intensity image as an input to a U-Net architecture of Convolutional Neural Network with a pretrained ResNet-34 encoder for image segmentation. The network was trained on limited-size annotated dataset to distinguish four classes in the images of thin sections of murine uterine cervix: background, internal os, cervical tissue, and vaginal wall. With only 74 manually annotated images in total (51 used for model training), the model achieved 90.22% pixel accuracy on the held-out test dataset. This framework requires minimal data pre-processing and is readily extensible to other tissue types, with publicly available graphical annotation tools for practical deployment.

title: Fair Like Us? Auditing LLM Alignment in Resource Allocation
abstract: Fair allocation of scarce, indivisible resources is an important challenge in many societal problems. While there are several formal theories of fairness, no single definition can always be satisfied. As large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to support decisions and act as agents, they raise new concerns about distributional justice: their judgments are not directly tied to any specific fairness framework and may violate key normative principles. In this work, we introduce a general method for evaluating fairness reasoning in LLMs. We study first-person fairness judgments across a broad set of models and compare them directly with human responses on matched scenarios and elicitation conditions. We find that LLMs tend to prefer stricter fairness constraints than humans, show more self-interested behavior, are sensitive to how information is framed, and are difficult to align with human judgments using fine-tuning with current datasets.

title: Latent-Space No-Arbitrage Geometry of Generative Models for Implied Volatility Surfaces
abstract: Generative models for implied volatility surfaces must produce outputs that satisfy static no-arbitrage constraints. We study these constraints in latent space. For a fixed generator, we assign each latent code a scalar margin determined by the no-arbitrage conditions of the generated surface. The codes with nonnegative margin form the admissible latent set. We establish conditions under which strictly admissible codes remain admissible under small perturbations and the boundary of the admissible set is characterized by zero margin. For regular boundary components, we formulate a level-set equation whose local dynamics are directed toward the zero-margin set. The analysis treats the generator as a map from latent variables to surfaces and is therefore not restricted to a particular architecture. It applies to variational autoencoders, generative adversarial networks, and other generative models with a deterministic realization map. Numerical tests recover known boundaries in analytic examples. Experiments with a variational autoencoder trained on Heston surfaces show that similar reconstruction errors can correspond to different admissible regions and that the latent prior may be concentrated inside such a region. The computed boundary can also be used to modify latent codes that generate violating surfaces.

title: Physical Adversarial Examples for Person Detectors in Thermal Images Based on 3D Modeling
abstract: Thermal Infrared detection is widely used in autonomous driving, medical AI, etc., but its security has only attracted attention recently. We propose infrared adversarial clothing designed to evade thermal person detectors in real-world scenarios. The design of the adversarial clothing is based on 3D modeling, which makes it easier to simulate multiangle scenes near the real world compared to 2D modeling. We optimized the black patch layout pattern of 3D clothing based on the adversarial example technique and made physical adversarial clothing using the aerogel. The idea is to paste a set of square aerogel patches, which display black squares in thermal images, in the inner side of clothing at specific locations with specific orientations. To enhance realism, we propose a method to build infrared 3D models with real infrared photos and develop texture maps for 3D models to simulate varied infrared characteristics over time and location. In contrast, randomly placed patches yielded much lower success rates (26.53\% indoors and 23.03\% outdoors). title: RSLM: Training-Free Vector Quantization for Approximate Nearest Neighbor Search
abstract: By introducing RSLM (Rotated Scaled Lloyd-Max), a family of training-free vector quantization codecs compressing embeddings to 1--4 bits per dimension, we reduce memory cost and memory bandwidth of a typical large-scale Approximate Nearest Neighbor (ANN) search system, while reducing its complexity and keeping or improving recall across multiple benchmark datasets. State-of-the-art systems filter candidates using coarse partitions, approximately score them to narrow the set, and then rescore the best with higher precision representations (often >=8 bits per dimension). Our relativized codecs can bring this down to 2--4 bits per dimension. We use the properties of the ANN system to encode residual vectors instead of full vectors, both for the approximate scoring phase and the rescoring phase. Since Maximum Inner Product Search (MIPS) is very sensitive to vector norms, we correct the $L_2$ norms of quantized vectors. Our major innovation is that we correct the $L_2$ norm of the final reconstructed vector rather than just the residual. Our rescaling replaces more complicated schemes, such as Anisotropic loss. The residualization scheme gives us a more favorable quality vs size trade-off than generic quantization methods. Our high-performance implementation leverages a block-wise cascaded Fast Walsh-Hadamard Transform (FWHT) with linear-like complexity, AVX SIMD-optimized codebooks, and a steganographic encoding of scaling factors for perfect cache-line alignment.

title: A Hybrid Graph and Transformer-Based Framework for Relational Identity Anomaly Detection in Digital Interaction Networks
abstract: Digital interaction networks are increasingly connecting identities, devices, accounts, and services, creating complex environments in which anomalous identity behavior can emerge. This study addresses the problem of detecting relational identity anomalies that conventional feature-based methods and individual deep learning models may fail to recognize. The problem requires attention because sophisticated identity attacks often exploit interconnected relationships, coordinated interactions, and long-range behavioral dependencies rather than isolated attributes. This study develops a hybrid Graph and Transformer-based framework that combines graph neural networks for learning structural relationships with Transformer-based self-attention for modeling contextual and long-range interaction dependencies. The framework fuses these complementary representations and applies anomaly scoring to distinguish normal and suspicious identity behaviors. Experimental results show that the proposed framework achieves 96.8% accuracy, 95.9% precision, 96.2% recall, 96.0% F1-score, and 97.1% AUC. These results demonstrate that combining relational graph representations with contextual Transformer learning improves identity anomaly detection compared with conventional machine learning, standalone GNN, Transformer, and existing hybrid approaches. The findings extend previous research by showing that structural and contextual information can jointly provide more effective representations for detecting subtle and coordinated anomalies in complex digital interaction networks.

title: Text-Level Distribution of Sentiment Signals in Persuasive and Expository Texts
abstract: Sentiment analysis has been widely used to classify or quantify positive, negative, and neutral polarity at the document or sentence level, but less attention has been paid to how sentiment signals are distributed within a text. This study compares eight persuasive and four expository texts, totaling 1,086 sentences, and classifies each sentence into an S layer or a Σ layer. Σ-layer sentences accounted for 69.2% of persuasive texts and 47.1% of expository texts. This tendency remained across additional statistical checks, although the small sample limits generalization. Σ-layer density was highly correlated with mean polarity intensity, indicating that it mainly reflects how frequently relatively strong sentiment signals occur. Future research should examine not only frequency but also the position, continuity, and transitions of S and Σ layers.

title: AI Conversational Systems: Evolution, Architecture, and Future Directions
abstract: Abstract Artificial intelligence (AI) has kind of emerged as a revolutionary paradigm, and it is influencing a lot of different industries, like healthcare education finance, and industrial automation. Chatbot systems, among its many applications, sort of act as an important interface that enables natural human–machine interaction, which sounds simple but is actually quite complex. This work provides a thorough theoretical analysis that ties together core AI concepts to more advanced chatbot systems. It looks at how AI progresses from symbolic systems toward data-driven models, then it extends the discussion into conversational agents that are powered by Natural Language Processing (NLP), Machine Learning (ML), and Deep Learning (DL). Along the way, the study discusses computational mechanisms application domains research challenges and also some newer trends, with a special focus on multilingual and low-resource conversational systems. The work kind of ends by outlining future directions for AI-powered chatbot systems, aiming for intelligence, ethical behavior, and context-awareness, even though people sometimes forget the last part.
