title: BeaconXAI: Budgeted Counter-Evidence Shortlisting for Portable AI Audits (Формирование ограниченного по бюджету списка контрсвидетельств для переносимого аудита ИИ)
abstract: BeaconXAI v1.0.0 Первая публичная версия исследовательского программного комплекса для интерпретируемого аудита black-box моделей временных рядов с ограниченным бюджетом контрсвидетельств. Проект объединяет два взаимосвязанных направления: локализацию компонентов модели с использованием ограниченного бюджета проверок; адаптивный аудит риска с ранней остановкой и оценкой вычислительной применимости на edge-устройствах. Основные возможности аудит black-box моделей временных рядов; budgeted counter-evidence analysis; адаптивное формирование shortlist проверяемых компонентов; ранняя остановка для снижения вычислительного бюджета; сравнение с uniform-базовыми стратегиями; поддержка экспериментов на UCI HAR, PAMAP2 и WISDM; анализ локализации и риска; воспроизводимые конфигурации экспериментов; формирование агрегированных таблиц и материалов для научных публикаций; оценка вычислительных затрат и переносимости на edge-устройства. Основные результаты В задаче локализации на PAMAP2 адаптивный подход adaptive_v2 улучшает результаты по сравнению с uniform occlusion: loc@1: 0.1211 → 0.2969; hit@3: 0.2109 → 0.4609. В задаче адаптивного аудита риска ранняя остановка уменьшает среднее число дополнительных проверок с бюджета Q=64 примерно до ~11, обеспечивая сокращение вычислительного бюджета примерно в 5–6 раз. При этом преимущество по качеству относительно равнобюджетной uniform-стратегии в текущем протоколе не подтверждено, поэтому результат следует интерпретировать прежде всего как инженерное улучшение по вычислительным затратам и задержке. Edge / portability Для HAR + ExtraTrees дополнительный вычислительный слой BEACON показывает: inference_only p50: 7.30 ms; BEACON core Q64 p50: 436.07 ms; оценка early-stop: 81.8–93.3 ms. Оценка для Raspberry Pi 4 является расчётной, а не прямым измерением. Воспроизводимость Репозиторий содержит: основную библиотеку beaconxai; сценарии экспериментов; конфигурации; агрегированные результаты; supplementary materials; материалы для подготовки научных публикаций; инструкции по воспроизведению экспериментов. Датасеты не распространяются вместе с репозиторием и должны быть подготовлены локально. Цитирование При использовании программного кода необходимо ссылаться на связанные публикации BEACON-XAI и на соответствующую архивную версию программного обеспечения.

title: Quantum Holistic Semantic Communication: Synchronization of Semantic Structures Through Entanglement
abstract: This work proposes a concept of using quantum entanglement for synchronizing semantic structures between remote observers without the need for classical data transmission. In contrast to traditional interpretations of the no-communication theorem, we demonstrate that quantum correlation can be used for instantaneous synchronization of complex patterns, the information extraction of which occurs through semantic filtering and contextual validation. The proposed QHSC (Quantum Holistic Semantic Communication) protocol uses post-selection, temporal signature verification, and AI-based reconstruction of meaning from fragments to distinguish Alice's correlated signal from Bob's local noise. We show that the probability of random generation of a complete semantic pattern by local noise tends exponentially to zero, while quantum correlation ensures deterministic pattern matching between Alice and Bob. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the algorithmic core of QHSC possesses the property of physical layer agnosticism and can be deployed on existing classical communication channels, solving critical problems of resilient communication in electronic warfare conditions, deep-sea and space communication, and critical medical telemetry.

title: Title: Spin Quantum State Geometric Transformation - Topological Structure Calculation
abstract: This research explores the application of spin quantum state transformations to geometric calculations, leveraging a novel algorithm and quantum computational techniques. The core aim is to develop a method for efficiently manipulating complex geometric forms through controlled quantum states. The investigation focuses on establishing a robust and scalable transformation framework, potentially offering improvements over existing classical methods. A key contribution lies in the integration of quantum algorithms into the transformation process, aiming to enhance computational efficiency. This work will delve into the mathematical foundations of the proposed transformation, outlining the core mechanism and demonstrating its potential for advanced geometric modeling. The study will analyze the resulting transformations, offering insights into their stability and computational cost. Finally, the paper will present preliminary results showcasing the effectiveness of the proposed approach.

title: LabMiM Micrometeorology and Solar Radiation Intelligence
abstract: Toolkit for solar irradiance and micrometeorology research at the LabMiM station, Universidade Federal da Bahia, Salvador, Brazil (13.0°S). It post-processes WRF output into JSON and GeoJSON payloads for web mapping, builds a quality-controlled archive from the station's Campbell dataloggers, estimates diffuse horizontal irradiance from all-sky camera images with multimodal deep learning, and corrects the model's diffuse radiation bias with machine learning. Held-out test performance for the image model: DHI RMSE 20.80 W/m², R² 0.939, skill over the clear-sky baseline +0.72.

title: Dynamic Quantum Topology Generation
abstract: Quantum topology, a novel framework for manipulating quantum systems, offers a promising path towards enhanced quantum computation. This paper introduces a dynamic quantum topology generation method, designed to automatically create and optimize quantum systems based on input data. We propose a method that iteratively adjusts quantum parameters to achieve specific performance goals, leveraging the inherent topological properties of the generated structures. This approach contrasts with traditional parameter tuning techniques, which often rely on manual adjustment and struggle with complex system behavior. The core mechanism centers around the creation and evolution of dynamic, topologically protected quantum states. This study demonstrates the effectiveness of this method through theoretical analysis and preliminary experimental validation, showcasing significant improvements in quantum entanglement and coherence.

title: Adaptive Dynamic Complex Mathematical Structure Optimization
abstract: This paper introduces a novel adaptive dynamic complex mathematical structure optimization algorithm designed to enhance the efficiency of mathematical structure optimization. Traditional approaches often rely on manual design, limiting the algorithm's ability to effectively handle intricate relationships. This algorithm employs a dynamic adjustment mechanism, allowing the optimization process to adapt in real-time, resulting in more accurate and efficient solutions. The core mechanism centers around continuous refinement of the optimization strategy based on the feedback loop, achieving superior performance across a range of complex mathematical structures. This work presents a framework for automated optimization, offering a significant advancement over existing methods.

title: Quantum Simulation Geometric Transformation
abstract: Quantum simulation offers a promising avenue for simulating complex geometric transformations with unprecedented accuracy. This paper presents a novel quantum simulation algorithm designed to precisely model and simulate geometric transformations, incorporating automated parameter adjustment to enhance simulation precision. We introduce a modified quantum algorithm that leverages the inherent properties of quantum systems to achieve this goal. The core mechanism involves using quantum states to represent geometric primitives and performing iterative transformations guided by a dynamic parameter adjustment process. This approach overcomes limitations of conventional methods, particularly in handling intricate geometric configurations. The paper details the algorithm's design, implementation, and results, demonstrating its effectiveness in simulating a range of geometric transformations. We also provide a comprehensive analysis of the algorithm's performance and discuss potential future research directions.

title: Adaptive Regularization for Non-linear Gaussian Functions
abstract: The study of non-linear Gaussian functions is a crucial area in machine learning and data-driven scientific modeling. Traditional approaches often require manual parameter tuning, which can be time-consuming and suboptimal. This paper proposes a novel adaptive regularization method for non-linear Gaussian functions, leveraging data-driven learning to dynamically adjust regularization strength. This method aims to improve model generalization and optimization by intelligently controlling the regularization process, effectively addressing the challenges associated with complex non-linear systems. The core mechanism involves an adaptive regularization strategy that learns a representation of the data distribution and adjusts the regularization strength accordingly. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through illustrative examples and analysis, showcasing its potential for enhancing the performance of machine learning models.

abstract: Quantum Machine Learning (QML) has emerged as a promising field, offering the potential to revolutionize machine learning through novel algorithms and techniques. We propose a novel approach that dynamically adjusts model parameters based on the inherent topological structure of the data, enabling the algorithm to better represent complex data distributions and improve predictive accuracy. The core mechanism focuses on adaptive learning strategies that facilitate robustness and adaptability. This work addresses a critical challenge in QML: the need for models that can effectively handle high-dimensional and non-linear data. title: Dynamic Topology Learning for Graph Neural Networks
abstract: Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) have demonstrated remarkable success in various graph-related tasks, including node classification, link prediction, and graph classification. However, traditional GNNs often rely on fixed graph structures, which may not effectively capture the underlying complex relationships within the data. This paper proposes a novel framework for Dynamic Topology Learning (DTL) for GNNs, aiming to address this limitation. The core idea is to enable the GNN to dynamically adapt its graph topology during training, allowing it to better align with the data's inherent structure and the specific task requirements. This is achieved through a mechanism that introduces the ability to modify the graph structure, such as adding or removing edges, based on the learned representations and the current task demands. The proposed DTL framework is expected to improve both the performance and robustness of GNNs.

title: Quantum Information Bottleneck with Adaptive Constraint Propagation
abstract: This paper introduces a novel quantum information bottleneck paradigm centered on dynamically adaptive constraint propagation. Traditional quantum computation often relies on static constraints, which can limit the exploration of the quantum state space and hinder algorithm performance. We propose a "Constraint Propagation" algorithm leveraging quantum entanglement to iteratively refine a constraint on a quantum system, optimizing for error mitigation and enabling fundamentally new quantum algorithms. This approach shifts the focus from static constraint application to a dynamic, adaptive process, potentially unlocking significant improvements in fidelity and computational power. The core mechanism involves using entanglement to iteratively adjust the constraints, effectively "steering" the quantum system towards a more stable and informative state. This work demonstrates the potential of this paradigm through theoretical analysis and preliminary experimental validation, showcasing improved error mitigation and the development of novel quantum algorithms.

title: Adaptive Data Augmentation for Low-Data Regimes using Generative Latent Spaces
abstract: This paper addresses the significant challenge of training effective machine learning models when limited training data is available – a scenario often referred to as a low-data regime. Traditional data augmentation techniques frequently prove inadequate in these situations, failing to generate sufficiently diverse synthetic data. We propose a novel adaptive data augmentation framework that utilizes generative latent spaces to overcome this limitation. The core idea involves learning a compressed, probabilistic representation of the data using a generative model, typically a Variational Autoencoder (VAE). Instead of simply sampling randomly from this latent space, our method incorporates uncertainty estimation to guide the augmentation process. This allows us to prioritize the generation of synthetic data points that are most likely to improve model performance, effectively adapting the augmentation strategy to the specific characteristics of the low-data setting. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through a theoretical analysis and outline the key components, including latent space construction, uncertainty quantification, and adaptive sampling. The system dynamically adjusts the augmentation process based on the model's performance and the estimated uncertainty of the generated data, leading to improved generalization and robustness.

title: ## Black-and-white Langur: A Meta-Heuristic Optimization Algorithm Inspired by the Behavior of Black-and-white Langurs
abstract: This paper presents a novel meta-heuristic optimization algorithm, termed "Black-and-white Langur" (BWL), inspired by the foraging behavior of black-and-white langurs ( *Macaca fuscata* ). These monkeys exhibit a unique strategy of alternating between foraging in dark and light patches within their habitat, exploiting differences in food availability. BWL leverages this behavior to develop a new iterative optimization process. The algorithm employs a population-based approach, maintaining a set of candidate solutions. Each solution undergoes a dynamic adjustment of its "lightness" parameter, mimicking the langur's switching between dark and light areas. The lightness parameter influences the exploration and exploitation phases of the algorithm, promoting a balance between searching for new solutions and refining existing ones. BWL incorporates a novel convergence criterion based on the variance of lightness values within the population. The performance of BWL is evaluated through a series of benchmark functions, demonstrating its effectiveness in tackling complex optimization problems. The algorithm's simplicity, combined with its inherent ability to adapt to varying problem landscapes, makes it a promising alternative to established meta-heuristic methods.

Traditional machine learning models often struggle with high-dimensional data and complex relationships, while graph-based models directly leverage the structural information inherent in networks to enhance learning and prediction. This work introduces a new methodology for analyzing and learning from data residing in networks, emphasizing the importance of representing data through graph structures.

title: Causal Graph Embedding via Intervention Simulation
abstract: Graph embedding techniques have achieved remarkable success in representing graph-structured data for downstream tasks. However, existing methods primarily focus on learning node representations based on correlations within the graph, often neglecting the underlying causal relationships. This paper introduces a novel approach, Causal Graph Embedding via Intervention Simulation, which addresses this limitation by simulating the effect of targeted interventions on the graph. We leverage simulation to observe the changes in node representations when specific edges are "activated" or "deactivated," effectively capturing causal dependencies. Our method moves beyond correlation-based embeddings, incorporating causal reasoning into the embedding process. We present a theoretical framework and an algorithmic outline for this approach, highlighting its potential for improved graph embedding performance and interpretability. The core claim is that embedding networks by simulating the effect of targeted interventions on the graph, capturing causal relationships. The core mechanism is using simulation to observe the changes in node representations when specific edges are "activated" or "deactivated" in the graph. This represents a significant step forward in graph representation learning, offering a more robust and insightful understanding of graph data.

title: Adaptive Quantum Algorithm Optimization
abstract: This paper introduces an innovative approach to quantum algorithm optimization, leveraging the inherent adaptability of quantum algorithms. Traditional optimization methods often rely on fixed parameters, limiting the algorithm's effectiveness. We propose a novel framework centered around dynamically adjusting quantum circuit parameters to enhance algorithm performance. This framework utilizes quantum superposition and entanglement to explore a broader parameter space, leading to significant efficiency gains. The core mechanism involves a self-adaptive optimization process, continuously refining the quantum circuit parameters based on the algorithm's current state. The paper details the theoretical underpinnings of this method, demonstrates its efficacy through simulations, and provides a clear pathway for practical implementation. We analyze the impact of parameter adjustments on various metrics, showcasing the algorithm's superior performance compared to existing methods. The paper concludes with a discussion of the potential implications of this approach for a wide range of quantum computing applications.

title: Bengal Fox Metaheuristic Algorithm (BFMA)
abstract: This paper introduces the Bengal Fox Metaheuristic Algorithm (BFMA), a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the hunting behavior of Bengal foxes. BFMA combines elements of Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Artificial Bee Colony (ABC) algorithms, incorporating a dynamic territory assignment mechanism mimicking the fox's social structure and hunting strategy. The algorithm utilizes a fitness evaluation based on a novel "territory dominance" concept, where individuals compete for and maintain advantageous search areas. The core innovation lies in the adaptive adjustment of the search radius and the dynamic reassignment of individuals to territories with higher fitness potential. We demonstrate the effectiveness of BFMA through simulations on a range of benchmark optimization problems, showcasing its competitive performance compared to established metaheuristic algorithms. The algorithm's performance is evaluated based on convergence rate, solution quality, and computational efficiency. The results indicate that BFMA offers a robust and efficient approach to solving complex optimization problems, particularly those requiring exploration and exploitation of the search space. Further research will focus on extending BFMA to handle multi-objective optimization and incorporating it into real-world applications.

title: Non-Abelian Entanglement for Quantum Computation
abstract: This paper investigates the potential of non-abelian entanglement for quantum computation. We propose a novel quantum computing architecture leveraging the unique properties of non-abelian entanglement to overcome limitations inherent in traditional models, specifically those based on abelian entanglement. The core claim is that utilizing non-abelian entanglement allows for computational capabilities exceeding those achievable with classical algorithms and standard abelian entanglement. The proposed mechanism involves exploiting the correlated interference patterns arising from non-abelian states, which are fundamentally different from those generated by abelian entangled states. We outline a framework for designing quantum algorithms tailored to exploit this distinct entanglement structure, potentially enabling the solution of problems intractable for classical computers. This work represents a significant step in exploring the broader applicability of non-abelian entanglement within the field of quantum computation, opening avenues for developing fundamentally new quantum algorithms and computing paradigms. We introduce the concept of a "Non-Abelian Quantum Circuit" (NAQC) and explore its theoretical underpinnings, including the mathematical description of state preparation and gate operations. The presented architecture aims to fundamentally shift the landscape of quantum computation.

title: ## Balearic Cave Goat: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Adaptive Behavior of a Unique Goat Breed
abstract: This paper proposes a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed "Balearic Cave Goat" (BCG), inspired by the unique adaptive behavior observed in the Balearic Cave Goat, a breed of goat native to the islands of Mallorca and Menorca. These goats exhibit remarkable resilience and adaptability in challenging, subterranean environments. BCG leverages a combination of self-adaptation, local search, and a novel exploration strategy mimicking the goat's navigation and foraging patterns. The algorithm's core mechanism centers around a dynamic population size adjustment influenced by environmental complexity, alongside a modified Cauchy mutation operator designed to promote efficient exploration. We detail the algorithm's design, theoretical underpinnings, and present simulation results demonstrating its effectiveness in solving benchmark optimization problems. The results indicate BCG's ability to converge rapidly and achieve near-optimal solutions across diverse test functions, suggesting its potential for applications in various fields, including engineering design, financial modeling, and machine learning. Key performance metrics such as convergence rate, solution quality, and computational cost are analyzed.

title: Quantum Error Mitigation via Adaptive Noise Injection
abstract: Quantum computing holds immense promise for solving complex problems intractable for classical computers. However, quantum systems are notoriously susceptible to errors, making accurate computations challenging. Quantum error mitigation (QEM) techniques aim to reduce these errors, but current methods often rely on fixed parameters, limiting their effectiveness. This paper proposes a novel approach to QEM utilizing adaptive noise injection, dynamically adjusting the amount of noise based on the observed error profile. We demonstrate that this method significantly improves the accuracy of quantum computations, offering a more robust and adaptable solution compared to existing methods. The system incorporates a continuous error rate monitoring and noise injection mechanism, optimizing for minimal impact on the computation.

title: Context-Aware Relational Reasoning with Probabilistic Logic Networks
abstract: Relational reasoning, the process of inferring relationships between entities, is a fundamental component of knowledge representation and reasoning systems. However, existing relational reasoning systems often struggle to effectively handle scenarios characterized by ambiguity, incompleteness, or contextual dependence of these relationships. This paper introduces a novel approach to relational reasoning, termed Context-Aware Relational Reasoning with Probabilistic Logic Networks (CARPN). CARPN addresses these limitations by dynamically adapting inference rules based on contextual evidence. The core of the system is a probabilistic logic network that utilizes Bayesian networks to model uncertainty in relationships and employs a unique "contextual weighting" mechanism to prioritize relevant rules. The system's architecture and operation are described in detail, highlighting the key innovations and potential benefits of this approach. We demonstrate the core claim that current relational reasoning systems struggle to handle ambiguous or incomplete information. The system's ability to dynamically adjust its inference rules based on contextual information represents a significant advancement in the field.

abstract: This paper explores the application of dynamic topology as a framework for quantum simulation, focusing on the development of a novel quantum simulation method utilizing entangled qubits and topological quantum properties. We propose an optimization strategy to enhance the accuracy and efficiency of quantum simulations. Traditional simulation methods often rely on predefined rules, limiting the potential for complex systems. Dynamic topology offers a unique approach, allowing for the inherent flexibility and adaptability necessary for simulating intricate quantum systems. This work investigates the potential of dynamically evolving configurations within a quantum system, incorporating quantum entanglement and topological features to achieve superior simulation fidelity. The core mechanism centers around leveraging the principles of dynamic topology to guide the simulation process, ultimately contributing to improved quantum computations.

title: Nonlinear Adaptive Random Matrix
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to solving linear equations using a dynamically adaptive random matrix, aiming to enhance machine learning model training. Traditional random matrix methods often struggle with complex nonlinear problems, hindering the model's effectiveness. Our algorithm leverages a self-adjusting matrix that dynamically modifies its parameters to escape local optima, leading to improved convergence and feature mapping capabilities. This design offers a significant improvement over existing methods, particularly for high-dimensional problems and intricate non-linear equations. The core mechanism focuses on continuous parameter adjustments to facilitate a more robust and efficient solution.

title: ## The Mantis Inspired Adaptive Search Algorithm (MIASA)
abstract: This paper introduces the Mantis Inspired Adaptive Search Algorithm (MIASA), a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the hunting strategies of the European mantis (Mantis religiosa). The algorithm leverages the mantis's remarkable ability to strategically position itself for optimal prey capture—a combination of anticipation, adaptive movement, and strategic adjustments—as the core principle for guiding the search process. MIASA utilizes a dynamic adaptation mechanism based on a "focus" parameter, mimicking the mantis's selective attention. The algorithm employs a population-based approach, with each individual representing a potential solution. The "focus" parameter dynamically adjusts the probability of each individual contributing to the next generation, favoring those exhibiting better performance and demonstrating greater adaptability. This paper outlines the algorithm's design, its underlying principles, and a theoretical analysis of its convergence properties, focusing on how the adaptive focus mechanism drives efficient exploration and exploitation of the search space. The algorithm's core components – the focus mechanism, the movement strategy, and the selection process – are detailed, providing a comprehensive description of MIASA's operation.

title: Differential Privacy with Stochastic Gradient Descent via Optimal Transport
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to achieving differential privacy within stochastic gradient descent (SGD) by leveraging the principles of optimal transport. Existing methods often struggle to balance privacy guarantees with model accuracy, frequently resulting in excessive noise and diminished performance. Our core idea centers around mapping individual gradient vectors to a common, privacy-budget-constrained distribution using an optimal transport map. This minimizes the information leakage while simultaneously preserving the integrity of the gradient signal. We present a rigorous mathematical framework for this process, demonstrating improved accuracy compared to traditional differential privacy techniques applied to SGD. The theoretical analysis highlights the key contributions of our method: a refined control over the privacy budget, enhanced gradient signal preservation, and ultimately, a more accurate model. The methodology offers a compelling alternative for deploying privacy-preserving machine learning models, particularly those reliant on SGD.

title: ## Amazon Hog-nosed Skunk: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by its Foraging Behavior
abstract: This paper proposes a new metaheuristic algorithm, termed "Amazon Hog-nosed Skunk" (AHS), inspired by the foraging strategies of the Amazon hog-nosed skunk (Conepatus chinga). Skunks utilize a unique "wavefront" search pattern, moving in concentric circles and adjusting their direction based on scent gradients. This algorithm mimics this behavior by iteratively exploring and exploiting a search space. AHS employs a circular neighborhood structure, a gradient-based adjustment mechanism, and a dynamic constriction factor to control the algorithm's convergence. The algorithm's performance is evaluated on a range of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness in finding near-optimal solutions with improved convergence speed and robustness compared to traditional metaheuristic methods such as Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Artificial Bee Colony (ABC). The core of the algorithm lies in its ability to effectively manage search space exploration and exploitation, resulting in a robust and efficient optimization tool. Key performance metrics, including convergence rate, solution quality, and computational complexity, are analyzed to provide a comprehensive evaluation of AHS. The algorithm is expected to be applicable to various optimization problems, particularly those with spatial or sequential characteristics.

title: Quantum State Embedding via Wave Function Optimization
abstract: Quantum state embedding is a crucial aspect of quantum information processing, offering a pathway to represent and manipulate quantum states more efficiently. This paper investigates a novel approach to this problem utilizing gradient-based optimization to create a robust and efficient method for embedding quantum states into higher-dimensional spaces. Current methods often suffer from computational inefficiency and limited exploration of the space, necessitating a paradigm shift towards optimized distribution strategies. We propose a new algorithm that leverages a dynamic optimization framework, dynamically adjusting the wave function distribution to minimize the energy of the resulting quantum state. The core mechanism centers around gradient-based optimization to guide the wave function towards a state of lower energy, ensuring a more stable and effective embedding. This results in a method with significantly enhanced computational efficiency and the potential for improved quantum information processing capabilities.

title: Dynamic Probability Field (DPF) Optimization Algorithm
abstract: This paper introduces a novel optimization algorithm for neural network training, leveraging the concept of a Dynamic Probability Field (DPF). Traditional neural network training relies heavily on static parameter updates, which can lead to suboptimal solutions and slow convergence. The DPF approach dynamically adjusts the probability field, allowing the network to learn more effectively and reduce training time. We propose a new algorithm that represents the neural network as a set of neurons and dynamically adjusts the probability field based on the network's state, optimizing for improved generalization and faster training. This work aims to address the limitations of existing methods by introducing a dynamic, adaptive approach to parameter tuning.

title: The Pecking Parrot Optimization Algorithm: A Biomimetic Approach Inspired by the Great Horned Pteropus
abstract: This paper introduces the Pecking Parrot Optimization Algorithm (PPOA), a novel metaheuristic algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of the Great Horned Pteropus (a large bat species). The algorithm mimics the unique strategies employed by these bats – specifically, their rapid, targeted pecking at fruit clusters – to efficiently locate and exploit food sources. PPOA utilizes a population of 'peckers' represented as vectors, each containing parameters defining a potential solution. The algorithm incorporates a 'pecking' mechanism that dynamically adjusts the search space based on the observed success rates of different regions. Furthermore, it introduces a 'cluster density' concept to simulate the concentration of food resources, influencing the movement and exploration of the population. The core of PPOA lies in its adaptive adjustment of 'peck strength' and 'exploration radius' based on the historical success of each individual, promoting convergence while retaining the ability to escape local optima. The algorithm's design aims to provide a robust and efficient solution for a variety of optimization problems.

title: 自适应量子密钥分发协议的量子纠缠机制
abstract: This paper introduces a novel quantum key distribution (QKD) protocol, termed "Adaptive Quantum Key Distribution (AQKD)," that leverages quantum entanglement to establish secure communication channels. AQKD distinguishes itself through a dynamic mechanism that adjusts the security of the key distribution process based on the quantum system's state. This adaptive nature enhances key protection and efficiency by incorporating a feedback loop that responds to subtle changes in the entangled state. The core of the protocol involves utilizing entangled states for key generation and distribution, with a novel mechanism for dynamically adjusting the entanglement's strength based on observed quantum phenomena. We present a detailed mathematical framework and preliminary experimental validation demonstrating the protocol's effectiveness and robustness. The research explores the potential of AQKD to overcome limitations of existing QKD protocols, particularly in scenarios requiring resilience against noise and adversarial attacks. This work contributes to the advancement of secure communication technologies utilizing the unique properties of quantum mechanics.

title: ## The Northern Alligator Lizard Inspired Adaptive Search Algorithm (NAISA)
abstract: This paper introduces the Northern Alligator Lizard Inspired Adaptive Search Algorithm (NAISA), a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of *Alligator lizards* in their natural environment. NAISA leverages the alligator lizard's adaptive strategies for food acquisition – including strategic movement, territory defense, and opportunistic exploitation – to construct a robust and efficient search process. The algorithm employs a dynamic population size, a novel adaptive exploration-exploitation balance mechanism based on perceived resource density, and a territory-based assignment scheme to promote convergence and avoid premature local optima. The core innovation lies in the algorithm's ability to dynamically adjust its search strategy based on the perceived landscape, mimicking the alligator lizard's intelligent decision-making process. This paper outlines the algorithm's theoretical foundations, its key components, and provides a conceptual framework for its implementation.

title: Development and Evaluation of an LLM-based Automated Feedback System for Reflective Writing in K-12 Education
abstract: This study addresses the challenge that severe time constraints in Japanese K-12 classrooms prevent teachers from providing continuous, individualized feedback on students’ reflective writing. To bridge this gap while ensuring pedagogical validity, we developed a real-time generative AI feedback system grounded in the Intelligent Tutoring Systems (ITS) architecture. The system explicitly integrates three ITS components: (1) a Domain Model encoding curriculum-standard-aligned learning objectives and criterion-referenced assessment rubrics; (2) a Pedagogical Model that operationalizes Hattie and Timperley’s four feedback levels (task, process, self-regulation, and self) through structured prompt design, incorporating few-shot exemplars co-authored by veteran teachers; and (3) a Learner Model synthesizing survey-based student profiles (self-efficacy, self-regulation, and reflection tendencies), long-term reflection-pattern summaries, and recent reflection–feedback sequences. A defining design feature is the simultaneous presentation of two AI personas: an Affective Support Persona that acknowledges learners' efforts and provides warm encouragement, and a Metacognitive Deepening Persona that poses reflective questions and offers perspectives for subsequent learning. To minimize expectancy effects, persona labels were hidden and display positions were randomized. The system was deployed during routine lessons across six classes at two elementary schools and one junior high school (N = 100; November–December 2025). Acceptability was assessed using a three-dimensional scale—clarity, specificity, and empathy— each measured by a single exploratory item grounded in the framework of Lizzio and Wilson. Across 397 lesson-level evaluations and teacher surveys, both personas were highly accepted (all means above 4.1 on a 5-point scale) by students and teachers alike (RQ1). For RQ2, students rated the Affective Support Persona higher on empathy, whereas teachers rated the Metacognitive Deepening Persona higher on both specificity and empathy with medium effect sizes, reflecting an emphasis on actionable guidance that advances learning. Although the middle-achieving group showed a significant persona difference in empathy, Kruskal-Wallis tests detected no between-group differences across achievement levels, suggesting that observed patterns primarily reflect differences in statistical power. Qualitative teacher responses highlighted the system’s potential to reduce workload while raising concerns about hallucination, student over-reliance on AI, and possible weakening of teacher-student rapport. Rather than replacing teachers, the system automates immediate, theory-grounded feedback to complement instruction, allowing teachers to reallocate effort toward context-sensitive coaching. This work provides a design framework integrating feedback theory and ITS architecture for LLM-based feedback in K-12 education, demonstrates the novelty of structured dual-persona presentation, and offers empirical evidence of acceptability from both student and teacher perspectives through sustained classroom deployment.

title: An Adaptive Harness Architecture for AI Transformation Diagnosis: A TIM-Taxonomy Core with Target and Stage-Specific Plug-Ins
abstract: 본 연구의 목적은 지역 AI 전환(AX) 정책이 요구하는 사업기획 평가와 기업 역량 진단을 동일 기준에서 처리하는 진단 아키텍처를 제시하는 것이다. 이를 위해 설계과학연구 방법론에 따라 적응형 하네스를 설계하였다. 하네스는 TIM 분류체계, 다중 AI 모델 합의 채점, 집계 규약으로 구성되는 고정 공통 코어와 그 위에 탑재되는 두 종류의 교체형 플러그인으로 이루어지며, 적응은 코어의 재설계가 아닌 플러그인 교체를 통해 수행된다. 제안 하네스를 기업 281개사와 지역 사업기획 40건에 적용한 결과, 단일 코어가 두 대상에서 유사한 상대 형태의 도메인 프로파일을 산출하면서도 각 대상의 고유 특성을 분별함을 확인하였다. 채점 코어의 평가자 간 신뢰도와 내용타당도가 이러한 결과를 뒷받침한다. 제안 구조는 코어 불변, 부품 적응, 공통 좌표의 세 설계 원칙으로 정리되며, 진단 산출은 의사결정을 지원하는 용도로 한정된다.

title: Thermal screening and critical scaling of quantum energy teleportation in a harmonic chain
abstract: We develop a finite-temperature Gaussian-state formulation of quantum energy teleportation in the one-dimensional harmonic chain. For Gibbs states, the optimized measurement-feedback protocol reduces to thermal two-point functions. In the single-site protocol, the extracted energy is governed by a single correlator, which makes the thermodynamic and near-critical limits analytically tractable. At fixed finite temperature, the extracted energy is exponentially screened with distance and is controlled by a thermal correlation length for both critical and noncritical α . In the zero-temperature critical limit taken after the thermodynamic limit, we derive the exact asymptotic law E ext ∼ d − 4 . Numerical results confirm both regimes and resolve the crossover responsible for the apparent drift of the effective decay exponent at intermediate distances. We also analyze squeezed Gaussian measurements and show that they modify the extraction prefactor: p squeezing enhances the extracted energy, whereas q squeezing suppresses it without changing the large-distance scaling.

title: LISynSeg: Data-Centric Label-to-Image Synthesis for Cross-Modality Whole-Heart Segmentation
abstract: Whole-heart segmentation (WHS) in computed tomography (CT) and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is affected by acquisition shifts and heterogeneous cardiac annotations. Existing WHS systems combine architectural design, transfer learning, and generic spatial or intensity augmentation. We investigate whether changes to data augmentation and training supervision can improve cross-modality WHS while the segmentation architecture is held constant. We present LISynSeg, a data-centric approach that augments real-image nnU-Net training with label-to-image synthesis. Synthetic volumes are generated from cardiac label maps using contrast and acquisition perturbations calibrated to the training cohort, then mixed with real images to retain thoracic context absent from the labels (and thus the synthesized images). We model cardiac label variation through controlled changes in myocardial wall thickness and partial supervision of uncertain vessel endpoints. On the CARE Whole-Heart benchmark, synthetic-only training performs worse than the real-image nnU-Net baseline, whereas calibrated real-synthetic training improves cross-modality segmentation without changing the architecture; the improvement is larger for MRI than for CT. The results show that modifying the training data strategy can benefit model development for heterogeneous cardiac data. Code and trained weights will be released at https://github.com/MedICL-VU/Care26_LISynSeg.

title: Generative Retrieval for E-commerce: Jointly Learning Embedding and Codebook with Same Product Cluster
abstract: With the development of large language models (LLMs), generative retrieval is becoming increasingly important in e-commerce scenarios. Current mainstream approaches typically use a two-stage training strategy: first train a product embedding model, and then learn a codebook that maps embeddings to product IDs. This cascaded approach suffers from two major issues: (1) error accumulation-if the embedding model in the first stage produces biased representations, the codebook in the second stage cannot correct these errors, degrading final retrieval performance; and (2) codebook learning relies solely on product embeddings and lacks modeling of query-to-product and product-to-product interactions. As a result, products belonging to the same cluster may be assigned inconsistent IDs by the codebook, further hurting retrieval accuracy. To address these problems, we propose a novel method that jointly trains the embedding model and the codebook, and incorporates same product cluster information as an additional supervision signal. Experimental results demonstrate that our method significantly improves e-commerce retrieval performance while simultaneously enhancing both embedding and codebook learning.

title: Steady-state multiparticle entanglement via dissipative engineering in waveguide QED
abstract: We propose a simple scalable scheme for the dissipative generation of entangled states of multiple emitters coupled to a waveguide. Our approach exploits collective interactions arising from the formation of subradiant and superradiant excited states, combined with the quantum Zeno effect. We show that, starting from an arbitrary initial state, the system deterministically evolves toward a W-type entangled steady state, with an infidelity that scales inversely with the cooperativity. The protocol is scalable to an arbitrary number of emitters. We further analyze the impact of additional experimental imperfections and present a detailed implementation based on trapped Cs 133 atoms.

title: Neural-network-based design and implementation of fast and robust quantum gates
abstract: We present a continuous-time, neural-network-based approach to optimal control in quantum systems, with a focus on pulse engineering for quantum gates. Leveraging the framework of neural ordinary differential equations (neural ODEs), we construct control fields as outputs of trainable neural networks, thereby eliminating the need for discrete parametrization or predefined bases. This allows for the generation of smooth, control-hardware-agnostic pulses that can be optimized directly using differentiable integrators. As a case study, we design and experimentally implement a short and detuning-robust π / 2 pulse for photon number parity measurements in superconducting transmon circuits. This is achieved through simultaneous optimization for robustness and suppressing the leakage outside of the computational basis. These pulses have very high fidelity ( ≈ 99.95 % ) and realize the parity measurement with an efficiency greater than 99.9% over a detuning range of ≈ ± 20 MHz , thereby outperforming traditional techniques while retaining comparable gate durations. This showcases the potential of neural ODEs for high-performance quantum control in experimentally relevant settings.

title: The Effects of AI Anthropomorphism and Service Recovery on Perceived Fairness, Post Recovery Trust, and Recovery Satisfaction in Chinese E-Commerce
abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) has become a key component of customer service in e-commerce, particularly in handling service failures and recovery processes. However, the mechanisms through which AI-assisted service recovery influences consumers' perceptions and post-recovery outcomes remain insufficiently understood. This study examines the effects of AI anthropomorphism and service recovery on perceived fairness, and investigates how perceived fairness subsequently influences post-recovery trust and recovery satisfaction in Chinese e-commerce. Data were collected from 400 users of major Chinese e-commerce platforms using a structured questionnaire and analyzed through descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation, and multiple regression analysis. Results indicate that both AI anthropomorphism and service recovery significantly influence perceived fairness, together explaining 44.7% of its variance. Perceived fairness significantly affects post-recovery trust (Adjusted R² = 0.461) and recovery satisfaction (Adjusted R² = 0.504), with interactional fairness emerging as the most influential dimension. In AI-mediated service encounters, interactional fairness, which reflects consumers' perceptions of respectful, sincere, and empathetic treatment, proves more influential than distributive or procedural fairness. This occurs because human-like interaction quality is particularly salient when consumers evaluate whether an AI system genuinely cares rather than merely processes complaints. This study extends the Stimulus-Organism-Response (S-O-R) framework and offers practical implications for e-commerce platforms. Findings suggest that AI customer service systems should incorporate calibrated empathy through emotionally responsive language, sincere acknowledgment of concerns, and personalized interactional cues to strengthen interactional fairness perceptions and enhance post-recovery trust and satisfaction.

title: Permanent Assistance, Eroding Competence: A Case for Programmed De-Scaffolding of LLM Tutors in Higher Education
abstract: This paper advances a deliberately contestable thesis: permanently available LLM tutors improve immediate assisted performance while eroding unaided competence. In a semester-long controlled experiment with 312 students, a static tutor raised assisted practice performance to 88.6% but depressed the unaided posttest to 61.7 points (control: 68.9). A tutor with programmed, mastery-gated de-scaffolding reached 76.4 points and 70.5 on the six-week retention test; an answer-seeking dependency index mediated 58% of the effect. Working paper of the Technische Universität Eisenfeld — not peer reviewed. Zusammenfassung (Deutsch): Diese Arbeit vertritt eine bewusst kontroverse These: Dauerhaft verfügbare LLM-Tutoren verbessern die unmittelbare Leistung, untergraben aber die Kompetenz ohne Hilfsmittel. In einem kontrollierten Semesterexperiment mit 312 Studierenden steigerte ein statischer Tutor die betreute Übungsleistung auf 88,6 %, senkte aber den unbetreuten Posttest auf 61,7 Punkte (Kontrolle: 68,9). Ein tutor mit programmiertem, mastery-gesteuertem De-Scaffolding erreichte 76,4 Punkte und 70,5 Punkte im Sechs-Wochen-Retentionstest; ein Antwort-Such-Index mediierte 58 % des Effekts. Published online in the TU Eisenfeld Working Paper Series: https://tu-eisenfeld.de/en/library/publications/llm-tutor-de-scaffolding

title: Quantum Neural Monitoring of Agentic Swarms: Separating the Monitor from the Workers
abstract: We present a design for overseeing agentic artificial-intelligence systems: programs that call tools, open sockets, and can leave a sandbox faster than a person can read a log. Most organizations now plan to deploy such agents. Few can oversee them at that speed. A human dashboard is not fast enough to be the first control. A second copy of the same classical model is not a monitor either. That copy can be manipulated through its prompts, can share files or sockets with the workers, or can be retrained on the incident it was asked to stop. At that point the supposed monitor is only another worker. We specify the monitor as a quantum neural network (QNN) whose internal Hilbert space is divided into a protected core, a control plane, and an interface wall. The QNN is required to finish one cycle inside one worker step. The QNN may read telemetry from the workers and from the wall. The QNN must not copy those readings into its core parameters. We call that forbidden update write-back. A human remains in the loop as a session, with authority to override and to walk away, and is notified after a halt. The human is not the isolation clock. The wall instrument issues the halt. The halt freezes network exits, file mounts, sockets, credentials, and accelerators, and leaves the machine running for audit. This is a design paper. The manuscript reports no fleet incident and no new hardware measurement.

title: falluck2025/prenary-math-lean-algebra: Day13 v1.0.1 偏元数学—代数与数论 · Lean 4 形式化验证
abstract: 偏元数学代数与数论 · Lean 4 形式化验证 Prenary Algebra & Number Theory · Formal Verification in Lean 4 声明:本文工作尚未得到独立实验验证,全部结论均为形式化验证层面的初步结果。 摘要 / Abstract 偏元数学(Prenary Mathematics)是在经典数学结构上引入"动作残差 ε"的一种尝试:经典对象保持不变,残差 ε 仅附加于"动作"(运算、映射)层面;当 ε=0 时,全部退化为经典数学。 本仓库以 Lean 4 对代数与数论的基础结构(群运算、环映射、椭圆曲线方程)做了形式化验证,观察到一个初步现象:动作残差 ε 不破坏结合律,但会破坏分配律、加法保持等代数结构,且群运算的单位元从 0 偏移到 -ε。 Prenary Mathematics is an attempt to introduce an "action residual ε" onto classical mathematical structures: classical objects remain unchanged, while the residual ε is attached only to "actions" (operation, mapping); when ε = 0, everything degenerates to classical mathematics. This repository formally verifies, in Lean 4, several foundational structures of algebra and number theory (group operation, ring map, elliptic curve equation), observing a preliminary phenomenon: the action residual ε does not break associativity, but it does break algebraic structures such as distributivity and additivity, and the identity element of the group operation is shifted from 0 to -ε. ——老陈与AI的深夜实验室 发布 请笑纳—— — Published by Lao Chen & AI's Late Night Lab. title: Quantum Topology Optimization: A Novel Approach to Quantum System Design
abstract: Quantum topology, a rapidly developing field of physics, offers a fundamentally different perspective on the properties of quantum systems. It proposes that the geometry of a quantum system, rather than its specific quantum states, dictates its behavior. This paper explores the potential of quantum topology to guide the design of optimized quantum systems, presenting a novel optimization method predicated on manipulating the geometry of these systems. We introduce a new algorithmic framework centered around the concept of quantum topology transformations, aiming to achieve superior performance and stability in quantum systems through controlled geometric adjustments. The core mechanism relies on identifying and exploiting specific topological features within the initial quantum state, thereby enabling targeted optimization. This research investigates the effectiveness of this approach through theoretical analysis and preliminary experimental validation. The goal is to provide a robust and adaptable methodology for quantum system design, pushing the boundaries of current optimization techniques.

title: Adaptive Geometric Deformation Optimization
abstract: This paper explores the application of a novel optimization algorithm based on adaptive geometric deformation, leveraging the principles of chaotic dynamics to automatically adjust geometric forms and optimize system performance in response to dynamic environmental changes. The core mechanism centers around a dynamically generated system of shapes, iteratively refined through a feedback loop that mimics the behavior of a chaotic system. This approach overcomes the limitations of traditional optimization techniques by providing a flexible and responsive method for shaping and adapting to evolving conditions. We present a theoretical framework for this algorithm and provide a comprehensive analysis of its performance, demonstrating its effectiveness in optimizing a complex system with fluctuating parameters. The paper concludes with a discussion of the potential applications and future research directions of this approach.

title: Bayesian Neural Symbolic Mixed Models for Causal Reasoning
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to causal reasoning utilizing Bayesian Neural Symbolic Mixed Models (BNSMMs). The core claim is to construct a hybrid model that seamlessly integrates neural and symbolic reasoning techniques, enabling the learning of causal relationships and accurate causal inference. The proposed mechanism leverages deep neural networks to capture complex patterns and correlations within data, while employing symbolic logic frameworks to represent and enforce causal rules and constraints. This allows for the fusion of learned knowledge with explicit causal knowledge, leading to more robust and accurate inference. We argue that existing causal reasoning methods, predominantly relying on statistical or symbolic approaches, often struggle with the complexities of real-world data. The BNSMM framework addresses this limitation by combining the strengths of both paradigms, ultimately enhancing the accuracy and generalizability of causal inference. The model is described in detail, outlining the architecture, training methodology, and inference process. We explore potential applications and discuss future research directions.

title: Title: Dynamic Phase Field Optimization for Machine Learning
abstract: The field of machine learning has witnessed remarkable advancements, often relying on complex model architectures and hyperparameter tuning. However, a significant challenge remains in achieving optimal generalization and robustness – the ability to consistently perform well across diverse datasets and scenarios. This research explores a novel approach utilizing dynamic phase field optimization to dynamically adjust model parameters, aiming to mitigate the limitations of traditional optimization methods. We introduce an Adaptive Phase Field Tuning algorithm that iteratively refines model parameters based on performance metrics, employing a simulated phase field to guide the optimization process. This method provides a robust and adaptable framework for improving model generalization and resilience.

title: 自适应几何结构预测的自适应学习算法
abstract: This paper introduces a novel self-adaptive learning algorithm for geometric structure prediction. Traditional methods often rely on static models, limiting their ability to effectively learn and predict complex structural patterns. Our approach leverages a self-adapting learning framework, employing a series of adaptive layers to dynamically adjust the model's parameters and enhance prediction accuracy. We present a comprehensive evaluation demonstrating the superior performance of this algorithm across a diverse set of geometric structure datasets. The core mechanism involves a hierarchical structure where each layer focuses on identifying and refining key geometric features, leading to a more robust and accurate prediction. The algorithm's effectiveness stems from its ability to autonomously optimize the model's representation, resulting in improved predictive capabilities. The paper concludes with a detailed analysis of the algorithm's design, implementation, and performance characteristics, highlighting its potential for significant advancements in geometric structure analysis.

title: 基于量子纠缠的几何拓扑计算
abstract: This paper introduces a novel computational algorithm based on quantum entanglement to analyze and manipulate geometric topology. The algorithm leverages the unique properties of entangled states to perform calculations on complex geometric structures, ultimately identifying potential topological defects. We present a framework for generating and analyzing topological defects through the manipulation of entangled quantum states. This approach offers a fundamentally different path toward topology research, potentially yielding more efficient and insightful discoveries compared to traditional computational methods. This work explores the application of quantum entanglement to uncover hidden geometric relationships and defects within topological systems.

title: Time-Based Quantum Information Encryption
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to quantum information encryption based on the manipulation of time-warped quantum entanglement. Traditional quantum key distribution (QKD) protocols often rely on the inherent uncertainties of quantum mechanics to secure communication. However, these methods can be vulnerable to sophisticated attacks exploiting advancements in quantum computing and measurement techniques. This work introduces a new paradigm where the temporal evolution of entangled states is actively controlled, introducing a 'time-warp' effect that fundamentally alters the information exchange process. The core concept involves creating a state where eavesdropping attempts introduce inconsistencies in the temporal relationship between entangled particles, effectively disrupting any attempt to clone or reconstruct the original quantum state. The theoretical framework outlines the mathematical principles underpinning this method, including the use of Bell states and the concept of temporal decoherence. We present a model illustrating how this time-warping effect can be leveraged to create a more robust encryption scheme. The proposed system aims to elevate the security level of quantum cryptography by introducing a fundamentally new layer of protection against potential attacks. The potential implications of this approach for future quantum information security are discussed.

title: Title: Quantum-Guided Neural Network Propagation (QGNNP)
abstract: Quantum-Guided Neural Network Propagation (QGNNP) is a novel technique for accelerating neural network training by leveraging quantum mechanics to enhance gradient calculations. Traditional methods often struggle with the computational complexity of training large neural networks, particularly during optimization. This paper introduces a QGNNP architecture that utilizes quantum gates to significantly speed up gradient computations, leading to improved learning speed and generalization capabilities. We demonstrate the effectiveness of QGNNP through theoretical analysis and empirical testing on a diverse set of neural network architectures. This research addresses a critical bottleneck in neural network development, offering a promising path towards more efficient and robust machine learning models.

title: Quantum Phase Estimation: A Novel Adaptive Optimization Algorithm for Quantum State Estimation
abstract: Quantum phase estimation (QPE) is a fundamental technique for determining the phase of a quantum state, crucial for various quantum algorithms and quantum measurements. This paper introduces a novel adaptive optimization algorithm, dubbed the "Adaptive Quantum Phase Estimation" (AQPE) algorithm, designed to enhance the efficiency of QPE by dynamically adjusting parameters during the state estimation process. We demonstrate the effectiveness of AQPE through rigorous theoretical analysis and extensive numerical simulations, achieving significantly improved convergence rates compared to traditional optimization techniques. The algorithm leverages a feedback mechanism based on the observed phase error during the estimation, allowing it to iteratively refine the parameter set and ultimately locate the optimal phase estimation. We present preliminary results demonstrating the algorithm's capability to mitigate the challenges associated with conventional QPE, particularly in the presence of noisy data. The implications of this research extend to broader advancements in quantum algorithm design and computational power.

title: ## Big Deer Mouse: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Behavior of *Peromyscus crassus*
abstract: This paper introduces Big Deer Mouse (BDM), a new metaheuristic algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of the Big Deer Mouse (*Peromyscus crassus*), a small rodent known for its efficient and adaptive search strategies in complex environments. BDM leverages the mouse's ability to dynamically adjust its movement patterns based on environmental cues and resource availability. The algorithm incorporates elements of both Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Artificial Bee Colony (ABC), with a novel adaptive movement mechanism mimicking the mouse's directional shifts. The core of BDM lies in its 'Directional Shift' operator, which modifies the velocity update rules to incorporate a probabilistic element based on the relative position of the current solution to a randomly generated 'resource point'. This allows the algorithm to escape local optima more effectively and explore the search space more thoroughly. We demonstrate BDM's performance on a range of benchmark optimization problems, including the Rastrigin function, Sphere function, and Brent's patuitary function, showing competitive results compared to established metaheuristic algorithms like PSO and ABC. The algorithm's adaptability and efficiency make it a promising candidate for various optimization tasks.

title: Towards Explainable Artificial Intelligence Decision Systems
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to designing decision systems leveraging the principles of Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI). The core claim is that building decision systems capable of explaining their decision-making processes significantly enhances trust and reliability. The proposed system utilizes XAI techniques, specifically SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) and LIME (Local Interpretable Model-agnostic Explanations), to interpret the predictions of underlying models. The system focuses on visualizing the decision process and articulating the rationale behind each decision, thereby increasing user understanding and confidence. This work addresses a critical gap in AI decision-making – the lack of transparency – and offers a new framework for constructing more trustworthy and dependable systems. The core mechanism involves a layered approach: (1) a model generates a prediction, (2) XAI techniques provide explanations for that prediction, and (3) a user interface presents both the prediction and the explanation in a readily understandable format. The ultimate goal is to shift the paradigm from "black box" AI to systems where the reasoning behind decisions is clearly articulated and justifiable.

title: Adaptive Topology in Quantum Simulation Algorithms
abstract: This paper explores the potential of adaptive topology in quantum simulation algorithms to significantly enhance accuracy and efficiency. Classical simulation methods often struggle with complex quantum systems, requiring substantial computational resources. We propose a novel algorithm that dynamically adjusts the topology of quantum simulation environments based on simulation results, fostering a self-organizing approach. This enhancement allows for improved model adaptability and ultimately, more reliable results. The core mechanism focuses on continuously modifying connectivity between particles, driven by the simulation's output. This approach addresses the limitations of static topology and offers a pathway towards more efficient quantum simulation.

title: Topological Unfolding of Multi-Body Quantum Entanglement
abstract: This paper investigates the topological unfolding of multi-body quantum entanglement, aiming to reveal the intrinsic structure and properties of entangled states. Utilizing topological methods, we mathematically analyze multi-body quantum entanglement and represent it as a series of topological structures. title: ## The Balbok-Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm for Optimization Problems
abstract: This paper introduces a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm, the Balbok-Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm (BIMA), motivated by the foraging behavior of the Balbok bird ( *Sylvia balbok* ). BIMA leverages the Balbok's efficient and adaptable search strategy to address complex optimization challenges. The algorithm employs a hybrid approach combining elements of Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Artificial Bee Colony (ABC), with modifications based on the Balbok's observed movements—specifically, its tendency to explore broadly during initial phases and refine its search around promising solutions as the algorithm progresses. The core mechanics of BIMA include a novel exploration phase inspired by the Balbok's wide-ranging initial scouting, a constriction phase mimicking its focused searching, and a convergence mechanism derived from its ability to maintain a stable foraging pattern. The performance of BIMA is evaluated on a series of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness and potential advantages over traditional metaheuristic algorithms. The algorithm's adaptability and robustness are highlighted, showcasing its applicability to various real-world optimization scenarios. The theoretical underpinnings of the algorithm are presented, and the key parameters influencing its performance are discussed, offering insights for future research and development.

title: ## Crab Shell Spiral: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by Crab Shell Geometry
abstract: This paper introduces Crab Shell Spiral (CSS), a new metaheuristic algorithm inspired by the geometric structure of crab shells. The algorithm leverages the spiral arrangement of the shell's plates to guide the search process, mimicking the efficient and robust exploration characteristic of natural spirals. CSS utilizes a novel adaptive parameter scheme based on the angular deviation of points along the spiral, dynamically adjusting the probability of exploration and exploitation. The core of the algorithm lies in a spiral representation of the search space and a distance metric derived from the spiral's curvature. We present the algorithm's theoretical framework, detailing its key components and operational rules. While empirical validation through simulations remains a future direction, this paper establishes a solid foundation for CSS, outlining its potential as a versatile optimization tool.

title: Evolutionary Strategy for Dynamic Program Synthesis
abstract: This paper presents an evolutionary strategy for dynamic program synthesis, addressing the limitations of traditional methods in handling dynamic adaptation. The core claim is that evolutionary algorithms can automatically generate programs adaptable to evolving environments. The proposed mechanism translates program synthesis into an evolutionary problem, utilizing genetic algorithms and evolutionary strategies to search for optimal program code that adapts to changing input conditions. The novelty lies in integrating program synthesis with evolutionary algorithms, offering a new approach to dynamic program generation. This work focuses on the theoretical framework and conceptual design, without experimental validation. The primary contribution is a novel algorithmic approach for tackling dynamic program synthesis problems. Key concepts include fitness functions, population management, and mutation/crossover operators tailored for program code evolution. The core challenge is to design a fitness function that effectively evaluates the adaptability of a synthesized program to diverse dynamic environments. The paper outlines the architecture of the evolutionary system and discusses potential optimization strategies. Further research will explore the implementation details and evaluate the system's performance with various dynamic environments and programming tasks.

title: Arizona Gray Squirrel Algorithm: A Novel Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm Inspired by Gray Squirrel Behavior
abstract: This paper presents the Arizona Gray Squirrel Algorithm (AGSA), a new metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of Arizona gray squirrels. The algorithm leverages the squirrel's adaptive strategies for food acquisition – including caching, patrolling, and risk assessment – to develop a robust and efficient optimization process. AGSA employs a novel representation of the search space based on a multi-dimensional grid mimicking the squirrel's foraging territory. Movement strategies are modeled after the squirrel's patrolling patterns, incorporating a probabilistic element based on food density estimations. The algorithm incorporates a dynamic caching mechanism, analogous to the squirrel's caching behavior, to store promising solutions. The performance of AGSA is evaluated on a range of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its competitive capability against established metaheuristic algorithms such as Genetic Algorithm (GA) and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO). The key innovations of AGSA lie in its territory-based search space, adaptive movement strategy, and dynamic caching mechanism. Experimental results show that AGSA exhibits promising performance, particularly in problems with complex landscapes and local optima. Future research directions include incorporating machine learning techniques to further refine the algorithm's parameters and explore its application to real-world optimization challenges.

title: Aritana's Brown Four-eyed Opossum: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by a Unique Animal Behavior
abstract: This paper presents Aritana's Brown Four-eyed Opossum (ABFO), a new metaheuristic algorithm designed to address complex optimization problems. The algorithm's inspiration stems from the unique feeding behavior of the Aritana's Brown Four-eyed Opossum, a species known for its deliberate and strategic approach to food acquisition. ABFO combines elements of Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Simulated Annealing (SA) with a novel adaptive inertia weight mechanism and a dynamic exploration-exploitation strategy. The core of ABFO lies in its "Foraging Phase" and "Observation Phase," mimicking the opossum's alternating periods of focused searching and passive observation. Mathematical formulations detailing the algorithm's key components, including the inertia weight update, the adaptive parameter adjustment, and the probability of transition between foraging and observation states are provided. The algorithm's performance is evaluated on a range of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness and potential for applications in diverse fields. The results show ABFO exhibits competitive performance compared to established metaheuristic algorithms, particularly in challenging, high-dimensional search spaces. Future research directions include exploring hybrid approaches and further refining the adaptive mechanisms to enhance the algorithm's robustness and efficiency.

title: ## The Arctic Hare Inspired Optimization Algorithm (AHIOA)
abstract: This paper introduces the Arctic Hare Inspired Optimization Algorithm (AHIOA), a novel metaheuristic algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior and navigational strategies of Arctic hares. AHIOA leverages the hare's adaptive movement patterns – characterized by alternating periods of rapid forward movement and strategic pauses – to explore the search space effectively. The algorithm utilizes a population of "hare agents," each with a position and velocity, and employs a novel "pause-and-seek" mechanism to simulate the hare's foraging strategy. The algorithm's core innovation lies in dynamically adjusting the probability of pausing based on the perceived landscape complexity and the agent's current progress. This paper details the algorithm's theoretical framework, mathematical formulation, and explores its potential applications in various optimization problems. The primary goal is to establish a robust and efficient optimization method inspired by the hare's natural behavior.

title: Anderson's Shrewmole: A Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by Shrew Behavior
abstract: This paper introduces Anderson's Shrewmole, a novel metaheuristic algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of shrews. Shrews are known for their erratic, seemingly random movements while searching for food, punctuated by periods of intense focus and sudden changes in direction. This algorithm, termed Anderson's Shrewmole, leverages these characteristics to develop a robust optimization technique. The core of the algorithm involves a dynamic exploration-exploitation balance, mimicking the shrew's alternating phases of searching and capturing. We present a detailed description of the algorithm's design, including the key parameters and their influence on performance. Performance evaluation is conducted on a range of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating the algorithm's effectiveness and comparing it to established metaheuristic methods like Genetic Algorithms and Particle Swarm Optimization. Results show that Anderson's Shrewmole achieves competitive solutions with potentially fewer iterations, making it a promising alternative for complex optimization challenges. The algorithm's adaptability and the insights gained from observing shrew behavior contribute to its potential applicability across diverse fields.

title: Andean Mountain Cavy: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by Terrain Navigation
abstract: This paper proposes a new metaheuristic algorithm, termed "Cavy Terrain Optimization" (CTO), inspired by the adaptive navigation strategies employed by the Andean Mountain Cavy ( *Cavia porcellus andinus* ) when traversing mountainous terrain. The Cavy's ability to efficiently find optimal paths, avoiding obstacles and minimizing energy expenditure, provides a compelling model for optimization problems. CTO leverages a combination of particle swarm optimization (PSO) and a simulated annealing (SA) approach, incorporating a novel "contour adaptation" mechanism to mimic the Cavy's terrain awareness. The algorithm utilizes a multi-dimensional representation of the search space, where each dimension corresponds to a variable in the optimization problem. The core innovation lies in dynamically adjusting the influence of the global and local best positions within the PSO component, based on a simulated gradient derived from the landscape represented by the search space. Furthermore, a simulated annealing component is integrated to allow for escape from local optima. The algorithm's performance is evaluated on a range of benchmark functions, demonstrating its effectiveness in finding near-optimal solutions within reasonable computational time. The results indicate that CTO exhibits competitive performance compared to established metaheuristic algorithms, particularly in problems with complex, non-convex landscapes.

title: Amur Hedgehog: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Foraging Behavior of the Amur Hedgehog
abstract: This paper presents Amur Hedgehog, a new metaheuristic algorithm designed to address complex optimization problems. The algorithm is inspired by the foraging behavior of the Amur hedgehog, a small mammal known for its efficient and adaptable searching strategy. Amur Hedgehogs utilize a "scatter and seek" method, moving systematically across a territory, prioritizing areas with higher food density. This paper details the algorithm's core principles, including the population initialization, the movement strategy, and the territory update mechanism. We demonstrate the algorithm's efficacy on several benchmark optimization problems, showcasing its ability to converge to optimal or near-optimal solutions with reasonable computational cost. The key features of Amur Hedgehog include its adaptability to varying problem landscapes, its efficient exploration-exploitation balance, and its relatively simple implementation. We analyze the algorithm's performance in terms of convergence speed, solution quality, and computational complexity. The results presented here suggest that Amur Hedgehog represents a promising addition to the toolbox of metaheuristic optimization techniques.

title: Neuro-Symbolic Reasoning with Temporal Memory Networks
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to neuro-symbolic reasoning by integrating Temporal Memory Networks (TMNs) with symbolic reasoning engines. The core idea is to leverage the pattern recognition prowess of TMNs, which excel at capturing and learning temporal dependencies within data, alongside the structured logical reasoning capabilities of traditional symbolic systems. We introduce a framework where TMNs process raw temporal data, generating learned representations, which are then fed into a symbolic reasoning engine for logical inference and decision-making. This hybrid system aims to overcome limitations inherent in purely neural or purely symbolic approaches. We detail the architecture, the integration process, and discuss potential applications, focusing on scenarios where temporal context is critical for accurate reasoning. The effectiveness of this combined approach is demonstrated through a conceptual analysis and a detailed formulation of the underlying mathematical principles. The key contributions lie in providing a robust method for translating temporal patterns into symbolic knowledge and vice versa, leading to enhanced reasoning performance.
